More than 4 million registered developers have chosen Mapbox because of the platform’s flexibility, security and privacy compliance. Organizations use Mapbox applications, data, SDKs and APIs to create customized and immersive experiences that delight their customers. 

What you'll do

This role is scoped by skill rather than by product. The problems below span multiple departments and show up across our Search and Places data work, our Location and Navigation Intelligence work, and the Platform work that makes Mapbox usable by agents. You'll be hired into one specific team or product area, but you'll work across teams where your expertise meets the highest-priority AI problems. You should expect to move between teams and tech stacks as the work demands.

At this level you own the technical design and delivery of a multi-component AI system, and you are accountable for the quality of what ships in your area.

In this role, you will:

  • Define how the products you own should work, build a measurement framework for it, and build evaluation systems for non-deterministic behavior. Formulate hypotheses around the products we build and seek the signal needed to validate them. Define what a correct result is for a given input and state, determine whether to assemble datasets from real usage or hand-written cases, and gate changes on regression results.

  • Run continuous evaluation of the products we build, whether APIs, SDKs, data representations, or reference applications, from the position of the end user, whether developer, agent, or consumer. Assess the gaps such as misuse of parameters or integration anti-patterns, recommend the fixes, and make sure they land.

  • Own the MVP against an agreed north star technical design, and balance technical perfection against shipping useful increments.

  • Build data pipelines and the tooling around them: ingestion, conflation, entity resolution, quality checks, and the batch and streaming jobs that keep a large dataset current.

  • Track and pull external datasets, models, and benchmarks from published research and open-source releases. Evaluate what fits the problem and constraints , and decide when to adopt what exists versus build your own.

  • Design feedback loops so that using a product generates data that improves it. Instrument systems so failures arrive with enough context to reproduce, then turn the recurring ones into evaluation cases.

  • Design the boundary between a model and the tools it calls. Build or improve the model harness, decide what the model handles, what it delegates, and how to keep it working from the state it actually fetched.

  • Work to a latency and cost target per request: streaming, partial results, caching, model routing, prompt structure.

  • Build the internal harnesses and tools (CLI, MCP, and others) your team needs to iterate quickly, and share the parts that generalize with other teams.

  • Raise the bar on your team through code and design review, and bring other engineers up on eval practice.

  • Some of the technical questions in this area are still open. You will help answer them.

  • Participate in an on-call rotation to ensure our systems remain available to customers 24/7. Team members alternate as the on-call primary responder, which may require immediate response outside normal working hours, including weekends.

What We Believe are Important Traits for This Role

  • Required Education/Certification:

    • Bachelors Degree in STEM discipline and 5+ years of software engineering experience, with production ownership of services, pipelines, or SDKs.

  • Technical Skills & Tools (Must-Haves):

    • 2+ years shipping LLM-backed features to real users, in systems that carried error budgets, on-call rotations, and customers who noticed regressions.

    • Data engineering depth: SQL, at least one distributed processing framework, and experience with pipelines where a wrong record mattered more than a slow one.

    • Fluency with tool calling and agent orchestration, including the failure modes: stale context, hallucinated arguments, silent partial success, unbounded loops.

    • Strong Python or TypeScript, and comfort reading code in whatever language the caller happens to be written in.

  • Core Competencies & Scope:

    • Direct experience or deep understanding of designing evaluations for non-deterministic systems. You can describe a dataset you built and the failure it caught.

    • Working knowledge of more than one agent harness, and opinions about where each of them is weak.

    • Experience diagnosing latency in a distributed request path.

    • Comfort with ambiguity, and the judgment to ship something narrow that works while the general solution is still unclear.

Nice to Have Traits for this Role

  • Geospatial data experience: routing, geocoding, POI or address data, OpenStreetMap, or conflation of overlapping sources.

  • Public API or SDK design experience, particularly for developers you never talk to.

  • Experience building against MCP or similar tool transports.

  • Automotive, in-vehicle infotainment, CarPlay, or Android Auto experience.

Most tools start and stop with dashboards. We start with the hard part: turning fragmented, messy enterprise data into a consistent foundation people can trust. Then we use AI to make it conversational, so anyone in the business can ask a question and get an answer they can act on.

We're well funded, growing fast, and have already processed more than £1 trillion of spend for some of the world's largest and most recognisable companies. Our partners use Deducta to deliver major business transformations orders of magnitude faster.

None of this works without the data. Every enterprise brings its own tangle of ERPs and legacy systems, and the usual answer is yet another integration. We think a new era of enterprise data intelligence needs a new way of thinking about data, not a new layer of the same plumbing.

You'll find new ways to reach and make sense of enterprise data, pairing the very best of AI with your own creativity to crack hard problems. You'll have real autonomy over how you approach it, in a small, high-trust team with genuine influence over architecture, product and how engineering grows.

What you'll do

  • Design, build and ship high-quality backend systems that power Deducta.

  • Work with customers to understand their problems, and bring fresh insights and ideas that shape the platform.

  • Develop reliable, scalable data and AI pipelines that ingest and process enterprise data.

  • Build internal tools and models that get more value from enterprise data and improve how we deliver our product.

  • Expand the range and depth of data Deducta can access, building a more complete picture of how large businesses operate.

  • Push the boundaries of applied AI, both in the product and in how we build it.

  • Own problems end to end, from definition to deployment, making sound calls on architecture, trade-offs, performance and reliability along the way.

Success in this role means:

  • Customers find deeper value faster: You find new ways to deliver speed and value to customers at scale.

  • Broader, connected data: Deducta can reach and link new kinds of enterprise data beyond spend, giving customers a fuller picture of their business.

  • Systems others build on: The pipelines and tools you've built are reliable, documented and used by the team without needing you.

Who you are

You're a senior backend engineer who enjoys hard, loosely defined problems and takes them all the way to production. You don't need a background in enterprise data or procurement. We care about how you think and the quality of what you've built.

You might be the right fit if you have:

  • Strong backend fundamentals and experience building reliable, maintainable systems, ideally with complex or messy data.

  • Sound architectural judgement, and the ability to explain the trade-offs behind your decisions.

  • A track record of owning problems from investigation through to production.

  • A solid grasp of software design principles. .NET and TypeScript help, but fundamentals matter more than a stack match.

  • High standards for testing, code quality and managing technical debt.

  • Clear communication with engineers, product, customers and external technical teams.

  • Real curiosity about applied AI, and the creativity to use it on problems others haven't cracked.

We care most about how you think, the quality of your work and how you approach unfamiliar problems. Previous startup experience isn't essential, but the pace, initiative and judgement to thrive in one are.

Hozah is a tech-led, award-winning company driving change in the parking industry and reimagining urban mobility. Our mission is simple but powerful: to transform parking into a seamless, automated experience, paving the way for smarter, more sustainable cities.

With recent recognition as PayTech Company of the Year, a place among Deloitte's Top 50 Fastest Growing Tech Companies in the UK, and significant VC/PE investment, we're one of the fastest scaling companies in the country.

Role Overview

You will own the Hozah data platform. At its centre is the BigQuery and Dataform warehouse: you'll model raw data into the management-information measures and KPI views the business runs on, and build the Metabase dashboards on top of them. We run ELT on managed connectors, so ingestion is yours too, but it is mostly configuration rather than pipeline engineering. The Pub/Sub streams and the Terraform that provisions them stay with our engineering team, and you request and review those changes rather than write them. You are the person finance, operations and the wider business go to when they need to trust a number.

This role exists because the platform has outgrown what one person can carry alongside everything else. Demand for management information has grown faster than ad-hoc effort can keep up with, and the business needs numbers it does not have to double-check. We are hiring a senior engineer to take full ownership, make those numbers reliable, and build the dashboard layer the business runs on.

You'll work alongside backend engineers on the source systems that feed the warehouse, and directly with the CFO, COO, Client Service and the wider leadership team as the people who depend on what you build. This is a newly created role with no direct reports.

In your first quarter, you'll agree one new data capability with the CTO, and take it into production over your first year.

Key Responsibilities

  • Own the Hozah data platform, from ingestion through to the dashboards the business relies on.

  • Take full ownership of the BigQuery and Dataform warehouse, including CI and the path a change takes from a branch to production.

  • Look after ingestion from source systems, mostly through managed tools such as Airbyte or Fivetran for SaaS connectors, alongside database replication and file loads.

  • Produce every department's KPIs from versioned, tested models, and deliver them on Metabase with no manual spreadsheet step in between.

  • Set and monitor freshness expectations for every ingested source, so a stale source alerts a named owner rather than surfacing in a board pack.

  • Work with the CFO, COO, CRO and other stakeholders to define and defend metric definitions, pushing back where a requested number would mislead.

  • Agree one new data capability with the CTO in your first quarter, then see it into production and adopted by a named business owner.

  • Be the platform's sole owner: triage issues, promote changes safely, and be the person the business trusts for numbers.

Who we're looking for

  • You've owned a data warehouse or platform alone, or as its lead, including being the one who fixes it when it breaks. You can say exactly what you were accountable for and what you personally changed.

  • You write deep SQL and model data properly on a cloud warehouse such as BigQuery or Snowflake, inside a versioned transformation framework such as Dataform or dbt, with CI around it. You can explain how you turned raw data into measures the business trusts, how a change gets from a branch to production, and what stops a bad one getting there.

  • You've made a disputed number trusted. You can walk through a specific incident from the last 12 months: how you found it, what the root cause was, and what now stops it happening again.

  • You work directly with non-technical stakeholders, and you've refused or reshaped a metric definition you thought was wrong. You can say what you said, and what happened next.

  • You've worked with at least one of change-data-capture or replication, SaaS connectors, or file loads, and know what tends to go wrong. Streaming experience is not required.

  • You've built the analytics layer yourself for business users (the measures, KPI views and dashboards), not just fed the data underneath it. You can describe something you built that changed a decision.

  • You've shipped one new data capability end to end, whether that's a machine learning model in production, a near real-time feed or a new data product. You can say who used it and whether it stuck.

  • You're comfortable setting your own priorities in a fast-moving SME, and you're happy being the only data person in the company.

  • Experience of GCP itself, Terraform, streaming, Kotlin or another JVM language, or Metabase is welcome, but none of it is required.

What We Offer

  • Hybrid working, 3 days in the office and 2 days from home.

  • Sole ownership of the data platform, reporting directly to the CTO.

  • The chance to build Hozah's data function from a working base as we scale.

  • A strong, high performing culture, with genuine influence over how that culture develops as Hozah grows.

  • A fully refurbished, modern office, right next to East Croydon Station (with a fully stocked kitchen, offering free breakfast, lunch and drinks!).

We're hiring a Key Account Manager to win new logos and then grow them. You'll find and open the door at landowners, managing agents, hotel groups and multi-site operators that have never worked with us, win their first site, and then earn the rest of their estate by delivering and building the relationship from the inside.

This is a target-carrying sales role for someone who loves the hunt. Rather than inheriting a book of accounts to farm, you'll build your own: the accounts you develop will be the ones you win, and the commission you earn on them is uncapped. Cold calling and outbound prospecting are a core part of the job, so it suits someone who enjoys both landing the first deal and then multiplying it.

You won't be running site go-lives, resolving driver appeals or chasing operational issues. Our Client Success Managers own the day-to-day running of each account, so your time goes on the commercial relationship, the next site and the next logo.

  • Own the growth of every account you win: map the estate, build relationships beyond the original buyer, and secure the next sites and additional services.

  • Hit your sales targets. You will carry a new-logo target and an account-expansion target, with commission on both.

  • Run a disciplined outbound engine: daily cold calling, email and LinkedIn sequences, event follow-up and referral asks, with the activity, pipeline and forecast recorded accurately in the CRM.

  • Run the full sales cycle yourself: discovery, site visits, proposals, commercial negotiation and close, with support from the wider team where a deal needs it.

  • Hand each new site to the Client Success Manager cleanly, with the commitments made in the sale written down, and stay the commercial owner of the relationship after go-live.

  • Hold regular commercial reviews with the accounts you own — performance, value delivered, and what else we can do for them.

  • Feed what you learn from prospects and clients back to the CEO, product and operations, so the proposition keeps improving.

We'll explore each of these during the interview process, so come ready with specific examples.

  • A track record of winning new logos in B2B sales, with the numbers to show for it: targets carried, attainment over multiple periods, and deals you personally sourced from cold.

  • A track record of then growing those accounts — not a career spent only developing accounts somebody else won. We want to see both halves: the first win and what you turned it into.

  • Genuine comfort with cold calling and outbound prospecting as a daily discipline, and the resilience to keep going through a run of rejections.

  • The ability to run a consultative sale: ask the questions that uncover the real problem, write a proposal that leads with it, and handle price and timing objections without caving or bulldozing.

  • Commercial judgement on deal structure — knowing when to hold price, what to trade, and when a deal is not worth doing.

  • Pipeline and CRM discipline: a real, repeatable routine for managing, prioritising and forecasting a pipeline.

  • Comfort working alongside an operations and customer success team, handing over cleanly and resisting the temptation to become the client's help desk.

  • Willingness to travel to meet prospects and clients in person across the UK.

Useful but not essential: experience selling to landowners, managing agents, hotels, retail or leisure operators, or in parking, property services, facilities management or another multi-site B2B service.

We ask a lot of this role, and we give a lot back.

  • You can translate a commercial strategy into disciplined execution: segment prioritisation, territory and account design, channel choices, target setting, sales capacity planning and the operating cadence required to make those choices work in practice.

title: Tech Ops Lead
description:
Hozah makes parking automatic. Our cameras recognise your car when you arrive and payment happens by itself when you leave. No apps, no tickets. We were named PayTech Company of the Year, we sit in Deloitte’s list of the 50 fastest growing tech companies in the UK, and we are expanding our estate of automated car parks across the country.

Every site runs on ANPR cameras, payment kiosks, edge devices and 4G connectivity, and all of it has to work around the clock. The TechOps team keeps that estate healthy. We are hiring the person to lead it.

The Role

This is a player-manager role, split roughly 50:50.

Half your week is leading our TechOps engineers: running 1:1s, setting standards, managing KPIs, coaching, and owning the service desk. You decide how technical problems get diagnosed and resolved at Hozah, and you hold the team to that standard.

The other half is hands-on engineering. When a client reports that revenue at a site has dropped 40% while every device shows healthy, you dig into the data, query the database, test the APIs and work out whether it is a bug, a misconfiguration or a camera problem. The systems are built in house, so there is no vendor to escalate to. TechOps own it through to resolution whether the problem lies in hardware, software or config and the fix is yours or a developer's. The software side is similar to L3 application support.

What you’ll be doing

  • Leading the service desk and developing a small team of TechOps engineers.

  • Personally investigating the hardest faults across cameras, networks, kiosks and our backend platform.

  • Using SQL, API testing and log analysis to get to the root cause of operational problems.

  • Improving monitoring and alerting so we catch degradation before it becomes an incident.

  • Technically assisting on new site launches: network design, hardware spec and commissioning.

  • Working closely with our Estate Manager, our developers and the COO to improve the estate week on week.

What we’re looking for

  • You manage a technical team today, or have very recently: real direct reports and real performance conversations, while staying hands-on yourself.

  • You have run a busy operation with high ticket volumes, multiple sites and live incidents, and kept on top of it.

  • You are an adept service desk manager: you know what to prioritise, when and what to escalate, and how to direct the team’s workflow so the queue keeps moving.

  • Your instinct is to investigate first: querying data, testing APIs, reading logs. L3 application support backgrounds fit this role well.

  • You have solid networking fundamentals (IP addressing, DNS, VPNs). Deep enterprise networking not needed.

  • You stay calm during live incidents and organised when several things need attention at once.

What this role isn’t

  • Corporate IT support. The users of our systems are cameras and cars, and the work is operating a distributed technology estate.

  • A pure management job. Half the week is engineering work, and we want someone who likes it that way.

  • Heavily process-bound. We are a scale-up, so you will build the processes we need as we grow.

Salary, location and working pattern

  • £50-60k depending on experience.

  • 3 days a week in our Croydon office, 2 days from home, with occasional site visits around the UK.

  • You report directly to the COO and own the new TechOps function.

The Role

This is Dust's first PM hire. You'll work closely with the product team, turning raw GTM signal, company priorities, and user feedback into well-formed problems the team can act on.

What you will change:

  • A lot of product signal doesn't reach the team in an actionable shape today. You'll create and run the process that connects signal to shaping to prioritization.

  • Implementing company strategies across functions requires ownership and orchestration. You'll translate company priorities into an intelligible, trackable set of product, marketing, and operations initiatives.

  • You'll enrich prioritized projects with distilled business and user context and market perspective so that the people building them make better decisions.

Our designers and engineers stay close to product decisions from conception to delivery. You're here to make their context richer and their priorities sharper. You enable distributed ownership, you don't replace it.

What You'll Do

  • Qualify and synthesize feedback: Sit at the intersection of GTM, users, and product. Turn high-volume, unstructured input into a small set of well-framed problems worth solving.

  • Shape initiatives: Work with engineers and designers to translate validated problems into initiatives ready for Stack Rank — with clear objectives, KPIs, and scope.

  • Drive outcome tracking: Own reporting on whether what shipped actually moved the needle. Feed that back into the next round of decisions.

  • Improve internal coordination: Connect Marketing, Comms, GTM, and Product — reduce the friction that slows things down when multiple functions need to move together.

  • Own outcomes, not outputs: For cross-functional initiatives, you'll own the goal — objectives, KPIs, orchestration, reporting.

  • Own artefacts in the Dust platform (agents, skills, data, etc..) to continuously rewire and augment the above for yourself and the team

What You Can Expect

Team

Dust is a growing team of about a 100 people. Most of the product and engineering team is based in Paris, with close collaboration across our teams in New York, San Francisco, and London.

The interview process

The process is designed to understand how you think, collaborate, and operate in an ambiguous, technical environment:

  • Recruiter conversation: motivation, background, logistics, and fit for an early-stage environment.

  • Hiring DRI conversation: discussion with a senior member of the product team.

  • Product exercise: collaboration exercise based on a real company priority.

  • Founder conversation: discussion with one of our founders on product judgment, attitude, and ability to operate with distributed authority.

  • Onsite: working sessions with members of Engineering, Design, and GTM. We’ll look at how you gather context, identify the important problems, collaborate on possible approaches, and leave ownership with the people closest to the work.

We care more about the quality of your reasoning and collaboration than about arriving at a predetermined answer.

What We're Looking For

  • Founding PM mentality: Senior individual contributor and builder balancing capacity to build the practice in the company while being hands-on.

  • 5–8+ years of product experience, including time at an early-stage company where you had to build process from scratch.

  • Genuine product taste. You know great from good in the world of tech products, and you bring deep perspective, judgment and conviction to any preferences you voice.

  • Excellent information synthesis skills, distilling a messy pile of customer feedback, sales calls, and Slack threads into sharp problems.

  • Technical proficiency earn the respect of engineers. You don't need to code, but you understand systems and tradeoffs easily deeply.

  • Builder mindset at heart. You use AI tools fluently and you're excited about what they unlock for how PMs operate. You've thrived in environments where everyone is a builder and you want to strengthen that.

  • Effective communication. You'd rather say one clear thing than three vague things.

  • Comfort with distributed authority. You influence by being right, not by being in charge.

Location

Pionnier des ventes événementielles en ligne depuis 2001 et acteur incontournable du e-commerce en Europe, Veepee collabore avec plus de 7 000 marques pour proposer des produits à forte décote, disponibles sur une durée limitée. Veepee a réalisé en 2024 un chiffre d’affaires de 3,3 milliards d’euros TTC et compte 5 000 collaborateurs répartis dans 10 pays.

📄 DESCRIPTION DU POSTE
  • Nous recherchons un Assistant Support Marque dédié et méticuleux pour rejoindre notre équipe. Le candidat retenu assistera notre équipe de support de marque dans leurs tâches quotidiennes, aidera les vendeurs à intégrer leurs catalogues sur la Brandsplace, fournira un support technique, centralisera les informations et mettra à jour la documentation.

    • 🎯 MISSIONS
  • Intégration des vendeurs : Assister l'équipe de support de marque pour garantir que les vendeurs intègrent avec succès leurs catalogues sur la Brandsplace.
  • Support technique : Fournir un support technique aux vendeurs, les aidant à résoudre les problèmes liés à l'intégration des catalogues, aux listes de produits et à d'autres problèmes techniques.
  • Centralisation de l'information : Centraliser et organiser les informations pour créer une base de connaissances cohérente et accessible pour l'équipe de support de marque et les vendeurs.
  • Maintenance de la documentation : Mettre à jour régulièrement la documentation interne pour assurer l'exactitude et la pertinence pour toutes les parties prenantes.
  • Collaboration interservices : Travailler en étroite collaboration avec d'autres départements pour recueillir, valider et documenter les informations essentielles à une intégration harmonieuse.
  • Conformité : S'assurer que toute la documentation est conforme aux directives de l'entreprise et aux meilleures pratiques du secteur.
  • Soutien aux meilleures pratiques : Fournir un soutien aux membres de l'équipe sur les normes et les meilleures pratiques en matière de documentation.
  • Amélioration des processus : Améliorer continuellement les processus de support et de documentation en fonction des retours et des besoins émergents.

    • 👉 PRÉ REQUIS
  • BAC+3 à 5 avec une spécialisation en communication, commerce ou marketing digital
  • Compétences organisationnelles et multitâches solides avec un souci du détail.
  • Excellentes compétences en communication écrite et verbale en français et en anglais (espagnol est un plus).
  • Maîtrise des outils et logiciels de documentation (par exemple, G Suite).
  • Capacité à travailler de manière autonome et en collaboration au sein d'une équipe.
  • Aptitude technique et capacité à résoudre efficacement les problèmes techniques.
  • Familiarité avec les plateformes de commerce électronique et les processus d'intégration de catalogues est un plus.

    • ✅ AVANTAGES
  • 👉Bureau flexible avec au minimum 3 jour sur place et jusqu’à 2 jours à domicile 
  • 👉Plateforme d’apprentissage des langues en ligne
  • 👉Comité d’entreprise CE et ses nombreux avantages 
  • 👉Accès à une restaurant d’entreprise et cantine connecté
  • 👉Accès à la salle de sport
  • 👉 Congés selon la durée du contrat

Votre rôle

Le Chief Engineer intervient comme référent technique et opérationnel multisite.

  • un référent opérationnel garant de la sécurisation des opérations ;

Vous travaillez en étroite collaboration avec les responsables de site, qui conservent la responsabilité opérationnelle de leur périmètre.

1 - Être le référent technique des infrastructures critiques

Vous apportez votre expertise sur l'ensemble des infrastructures techniques du Data Center et êtes capable d'en comprendre les interactions et les impacts opérationnels.

  • les UPS / onduleurs ;

  • les groupes électrogènes ;

  • les infrastructures CVC / HVAC ;

  • les systèmes de refroidissement ;

  • la protection et la sécurité incendie ;

  • les systèmes de contrôle-commande et infrastructures associées.

Vous intervenez comme référent technique auprès des responsables de site et des équipes Operations, et êtes capable de challenger les différents interlocuteurs internes ou externes sur leurs choix et leurs pratiques.

L'une de vos responsabilités majeures sera de garantir que les opérations réalisées sur les infrastructures critiques sont préparées et exécutées dans les meilleures conditions de sécurité et de maîtrise des risques.

L'un des enjeux majeurs du poste est de contribuer à l'harmonisation des pratiques entre les différents sites.

Aujourd'hui, les niveaux de maturité et les pratiques peuvent varier d'un site à l'autre. Votre rôle sera de contribuer à construire un socle commun de méthodes et de standards opérationnels.

Vous serez notamment amené(e) à :

  • définir et harmoniser les standards techniques ;

  • rédiger et améliorer les procédures et modes opératoires ;

  • mettre en place des workflows opérationnels ;

  • identifier les écarts entre les sites ;

  • proposer et suivre les plans d'amélioration ;

  • partager les bonnes pratiques ;

  • réaliser des REX multisites ;

  • accompagner les équipes dans l'adoption des nouveaux standards.

La capacité à construire et faire vivre des process sera donc aussi importante que votre expertise technique.

4- Apporter votre expertise lors des incidents critiques

En cas d'incident technique complexe, vous intervenez comme référent technique auprès des équipes Facility et Operations.

Vous êtes notamment amené(e) à :

  • analyser techniquement l'incident ;

  • identifier les causes et les impacts potentiels ;

  • apporter votre expertise aux responsables de site ;

  • challenger les analyses proposées ;

  • accompagner les équipes internes et les prestataires ;

  • contribuer à la définition des actions correctives ;

description:
Contexte :

ENSTA est un établissement d’enseignement supérieur et de recherche sous tutelle du ministère des Armées. L’école a pour mission la formation d’élèves ingénieurs civils et militaires, dont les ingénieurs de l'armement et les ingénieurs des études et techniques de l'armement, ainsi que des cadres et docteurs hautement qualifiés pour les secteurs public et privé, en particulier dans les domaines de la défense et de la sécurité, des transports, de l'énergie, des activités maritimes, du numérique et des technologies de pointe.

 

ENSTA accompagne par sa recherche, son innovation et son offre de formation la transformation des grands secteurs stratégiques nationaux répondant ainsi aux enjeux de souveraineté nationale. Elle dispose de 3 unités de formation et de recherche (UFR) organisées autour de 9 laboratoires de recherche (UER) qui mènent une recherche appliquée en relation étroite avec l’industrie.

 

ENSTA est membre fondateur de l’Institut Polytechnique de Paris (IP Paris). Dans le cadre d’IP Paris, l’école participe aux activités des centres interdisciplinaires notamment du centre interdisciplinaire d'études pour la Défense et la Sécurité (CIEDS, soutenu par le ministère des armées et l’agence de l’innovation de défense (AID)). Elle est à l’origine de la création du Centre interdisciplinaire Mers & Océans, inauguré en janvier 2025. Des chercheurs de l’école travaillent également en collaboration dans le cadre d'études portées par les centres Hi-Paris, lauréat en 2024 IA Cluster, E4C ou E4H notamment.

ENSTA résulte de la fusion le 1er janvier 2025 d’ENSTA Paris et d’ENSTA Bretagne.  Son siège est situé à Palaiseau (91), sur le campus de Paris-Saclay et elle a un autre campus à Brest. Elle met en place une nouvelle formation d’ingénieur unifiée sur les deux campus (Paris-Saclay et Brest) à la rentrée académique 2026/2027.

 

Rejoindre l'école, c'est intégrer un établissement engagé pour la parité et l'égalité professionnelle, la diversité et l'accompagnement de ses agents en situation de handicap, dès le recrutement et tout au long de la carrière. Afin de préserver le bien-être au travail, l'école mène une politique active en matière de conditions de travail, reposant notamment sur un juste équilibre entre vie personnelle et vie professionnelle.

 

Sujet : « Artificial Intelligence for Sustainable Renewable Energy Production and Storage in Subsurface Reservoirs”

Ce poste fait partie de la subvention « Leveraging AI for Sustainable Renewable Energy Production and Storage », financée par Hi ! Paris (https://www.hi-paris.fr/). La recherche sera menée à l'ENSTA, Institut Polytechnique de Paris. Le poste offre l'opportunité de travailler sur un sujet de recherche stimulant et impactant. Les connaissances, l'innovation et les compétences développées dans le cadre de ce poste offriront d'excellentes perspectives d'évolution de carrière tant dans l'industrie que dans le monde universitaire.

Le changement climatique exige des stratégies innovantes pour exploiter les énergies renouvelables. Le sous-sol de la Terre offre un potentiel important grâce à des technologies telles que l'énergie géothermique profonde, le stockage souterrain de l'hydrogène et le captage, l'utilisation et le stockage du carbone (CCUS). Ces méthodes pourraient transformer le paysage énergétique de la France et de l'Europe, mais elles sont souvent entravées par la sismicité induite par l'injection de fluides dans la croûte terrestre.

Pour relever ce défi, il faut des solutions avancées. La théorie du contrôle mathématique, telle qu'explorée dans le projet INJECT du CER (https://cordis.europa.eu/project/id/101087771), offre des stratégies pour minimiser les risques sismiques tout en optimisant la production d'énergie. Par ailleurs, l'intelligence artificielle (IA), en particulier l'apprentissage par renforcement (AR), présente une approche transformatrice grâce à sa nature agnostique et orientée vers la performance. L'apprentissage par renforcement peut développer des politiques très efficaces pour la gestion des systèmes souterrains et sert de paradigme pour aborder des systèmes complexes avec des incertitudes et des contraintes similaires, débloquant ainsi des applications plus larges dans divers domaines. Pour plus d'informations, veuillez contacter : ----- class="Default" style="text-align:justify;">Missions / Activités principales :

En tant que post-doctorant, vous ferez progresser les méthodes d'intelligence artificielle pour relever les défis du monde réel en matière de contrôle des systèmes régis par des équations différentielles partielles (EDP) non linéaires et non lisses. Les objectifs clés comprennent le développement d'algorithmes RL robustes, stables et adaptables, qui peuvent améliorer les modèles prédictifs pour la sismicité induite, le contrôle et l'optimisation de la production.

Le poste met l'accent sur la recherche interdisciplinaire, en intégrant l'IA à la géomécanique et à la théorie du contrôle pour approfondir la compréhension scientifique de l'injection de fluides dans le sous-sol et de la mécanique des tremblements de terre. Les résultats contribueront à des avancées scientifiques de pointe ayant un impact sur les communautés universitaires et industrielles.

description:
Angefangen hat alles vor sieben Jahren als ambitionierte Idee. Heute sind wir Marktführer für Abschlusszeitungen in Deutschland. Unsere Mission: Durch digitale Innovation und persönlichen Kundenkontakt sind wir für SchülerInnen der verlässliche Partner bei ihrem allerersten großen Projekt. Dafür hinterfragen wir permanent den Status Quo und entwickeln neue, kreative Lösungen.

Wir sind ein kleines Team mit sehr großer Reichweite. Unsere Kunden sind SchülerInnen, die gerade ihre Abizeitung oder ihre Abschlusstextilien planen. Für viele ist das ihr erstes großes Projekt. Im Kundensupport (m/w/d) bist du ihre erste Anlaufstelle: per Chat, Telefon und Videocall, von der ersten Frage bis zur Lieferung. Standardfragen beantworten bei uns Chatbot und Helpcenter, du bist überall da, wo ein Mensch gebraucht wird. Das heißt viel direkter Kontakt, schnelles Feedback und echte Verantwortung.

Aufgaben

  • Support: Du beantwortest Anfragen unserer SchülerInnen per Chat, Telefon und E-Mail. Schnell, freundlich und so, dass sie danach wirklich weiterkommen.

  • Problemlösung: Wenn etwas hakt, etwa bei Freigaben, Bestellungen oder Lieferterminen, findest du gemeinsam mit unserem Operations-Team eine Lösung und hältst den Jahrgang auf dem Laufenden.

  • Begleitung: Du begleitest Jahrgänge von der Angebotsannahme bis zur Lieferung und sorgst dafür, dass kein Projekt untergeht.

  • Video-Sprechstunden: Du führst buchbare Video-Calls, in denen SchülerInnen intensive Unterstützung bei ihrem Projekt bekommen.

  • Self-Service: Du erkennst, welche Fragen immer wiederkommen, und hilfst dabei, Chatbot und Helpcenter besser zu machen.

  • Feedback: Du gibst weiter, was SchülerInnen bewegt, damit wir Produkt und Abläufe verbessern können.

So arbeiten wir

  • Wir sprechen die Sprache unserer Kunden. Unsere Kunden sind 17, 18 oder 19 Jahre alt. Sie melden sich nach der Schule, in der Pause oder kurz vor der Deadline. Sie brauchen jemanden, der geduldig erklärt, verlässlich zurückmeldet und ehrlich sagt, wenn es eng wird.

  • Automatisierung entlastet dich, sie ersetzt dich nicht. Chatbot, Helpcenter und Onboarding-Videos nehmen dir die Standardfragen ab, damit du Zeit für die Gespräche hast, die wirklich zählen.

  • Eigeninitiative ist Pflicht, nicht Bonus. Du bekommst Ziele und Kontext, den Weg gestaltest du selbst. Niemand treibt dich an, aber alle verlassen sich auf dich.

  • Hybrid, ehrlich gemeint. Unser neues Office liegt im Mindspace in der Uhlandstraße 32, direkt am Kudamm und bestens angebunden, mit allen Annehmlichkeiten eines Coworking Space. Alle weiteren Mindspace Standorte kannst du temporär mitnutzen. Homeoffice und mobiles Arbeiten sind selbstverständlich möglich, solange das Ergebnis stimmt.

Qualifikation

  • Du hast Erfahrung im Kundenservice oder Support, idealerweise mit Endkunden. Quereinstieg ist ausdrücklich willkommen, etwa aus Hospitality, Hotellerie, Gastronomie, Einzelhandel oder Jugendarbeit.

  • Du kannst gut mit jungen Menschen: locker im Ton, verbindlich in der Sache und geduldig, wenn dieselbe Frage zum dritten Mal kommt.

  • Du schreibst schnell, klar und freundlich. Am Telefon bist du genauso entspannt wie im Chat.

  • Du behältst auch bei vielen parallelen Anfragen den Überblick. Unsere Saison hat klare Peaks.

  • Du lieferst zuverlässig und meldest dich, bevor jemand nachfragen muss.

  • Du arbeitest sicher mit digitalen Tools wie Chat-, Ticket- oder CRM-Systemen.

  • Du sprichst fließend Deutsch. Das ist bei uns Voraussetzung, weil unsere Kunden deutschsprachig sind.

  • Du hast eine proaktive Haltung und arbeitest gerne eng mit anderen Teams zusammen.

Benefits

Unser Angebot

  • Du begleitest jedes Jahr Abschlussjahrgänge aus ganz Deutschland bei ihrem allerersten großen Projekt

  • Eine Rolle mit Perspektive: Wenn du willst, übernimmst du Schritt für Schritt mehr Verantwortung

  • Ein kleines Team, in dem deine Arbeit direkt sichtbar ist

  • Kurze Wege und offene Ohren: Ideen landen bei uns direkt beim Entscheider, ohne Zwischenebenen

  • 30 Urlaubstage, Firmenlaptop, Sachgutscheine sowie D-Ticket oder JobRad

Die perfekte Bewerberin oder den perfekten Bewerber gibt es nicht. Wir freuen uns auf deine Bewerbung, auch wenn du die Anforderungen (noch) nicht zu 100 % erfüllst, du aber die Motivation mitbringst, dir die nötigen Fähigkeiten anzueignen. title: Team Lead Fuselage, Doors & Windows (all genders)
description:
Your Mission:

As Team Lead Fuselage, Doors & Windows (all genders) in our Structures Team, you will lead the structural design and development of VÆRIDION’s fuselage, door, and windows work packages for our CS-23 all-electric aircraft.

Your mission is to guide a small team of engineers in delivering lightweight, manufacturable, certifiable, and production-ready structural solutions. You will be responsible for technical direction, work-package execution, team coordination, cross-functional alignment, and delivery quality within your scope.

This role combines hands-on aircraft structures expertise with strong leadership. You will not only execute engineering work yourself, but also enable others, remove blockers, anticipate risks, and represent the Structures function in internal and external discussions.

 

Your Day-to-Day:

  • Lead complete fuselage, doors, and windows work packages independently.

  • Manage, coach, and develop a small team of structures engineers.

  • Set priorities, assign tasks, track progress, and ensure high-quality delivery.

  • Own technical coordination for fuselage structures, door surrounds, window cut-outs, reinforcements, fittings, interfaces, and installations.

  • Drive design maturity from concept through detailed design, prototype build, test support, and production release.

  • Anticipate and mitigate technical, schedule, manufacturing, supplier, and certification risks.

  • Represent Structures in cross-functional meetings, design reviews, supplier reviews, and certification discussions.

  • Align stakeholders across Stress, Systems, Production, Certification, Quality, Procurement, and external partners.

  • Challenge assumptions, bring practical design improvements, and help the team make sound technical decisions.

  • Review key engineering outputs, including CAD models, drawings, interface definitions, and design documentation.

  • Build team capability by improving methods, standards, templates, and ways of working.

 

Your Profile:

  • Degree in Mechanical Engineering, Aerospace Engineering, or a related discipline.

  • 10+ years of aerospace structural design experience.

  • Proven experience leading technical work packages and coordinating engineering teams.

  • Strong leadership skills: clear communication, prioritization, decision-making, conflict resolution, and team development.

  • Experience in at least two full aircraft development programs, such as clean-sheet aircraft, major modifications, prototype-to-certification programs, or production ramp-ups.

  • Strong experience with metallic fuselage structures, aircraft doors, windows, cut-outs, reinforcements, fittings, interfaces, or major airframe assemblies.

  • Strong understanding of metallic and composite aircraft structures, load paths, manufacturability, inspectability, repairability, and certification constraints.

  • Deep proficiency in CATIA V5 or 3DX and configuration-controlled design data.

  • Solid understanding of airworthiness and certification principles related to aircraft structures, ideally including EASA CS-23.

  • Ability to anticipate risks, create clarity, align stakeholders, and deliver results through others.

  • Confidence to represent the function internally and externally.

  • Be part of an ambitious team determined to shape the future of aviation.

  • We are an in-office company, but we value flexibility and trust employees to manage their schedules responsibly. This may include occasional remote work or adjusting hours to accommodate personal commitments.

  • Subsidized EGYM Wellpass membership: your (mental) health is important for us.

  • Lease a high-quality bicycle or e-bike through our JobRad program and benefit from tax advantages. Whether for your daily commute or personal use, enjoy more mobility and sustainability.

  • Pension scheme to support your long-term financial security.

  • Work in one of our offices in Munich or Delft. Enjoy the modern Balan Campus in Munich or work inside the aerospace ecosystem at TU Delft.

  • Boost your professional as well as personal growth executing your own ideas and independent projects.

  • Join our internal social events and retreats (e.g. cooking, game nights, sports).

Orbem uses AI to industrialize MRI, delivering non-invasive insight into everything from fruits to eggs to the human body. Orbem is at a critical inflection point. As we scale our range of unique products, we need delivery that is predictable, transparent and built to scale.

As a Staff Technical Program Manager within our TPM team, you will drive the delivery of complex, high-stakes programs that bring our products from development to market. Experience with deep-tech products involving AI or MRI — or direct exposure to the Food & Fresh Produce industry, particularly melons or soft fruits — is a significant plus. description:

Unbefristet · Vollzeit · Start ab sofort · Berlin, 2 Tage pro Woche im Office

Starte deine Sales-Karriere bei Pennylane in Berlin. Als Junior Sales Manager (intern: Sales Development Representative) arbeitest du 100 % Inbound: Du sprichst mit Unternehmen, die bereits Interesse an unserer Software gezeigt haben, klärst ihren Bedarf und vereinbarst passende Demo-Termine für unsere Account Executives – ohne Kaltakquise. Mit Sales Academy, Buddy und Shadowing lernst du den SaaS-Vertrieb von Grund auf.

Du willst Arbeit, die etwas bewirkt – an einem Produkt, das bald Millionen von Unternehmer:innen in Europa helfen könnte?

Du arbeitest am besten in einer Kultur, die auf Vertrauen und Eigenverantwortung setzt?

Dann könnte Pennylane genau der richtige Ort für dich sein.

Unsere Vision

Unser Ziel ist es, die beliebteste Finanzmanagement-Software für KMU in Europa zu werden.

Wir befreien Unternehmer:innen von zeitraubenden Aufgaben in Buchhaltung und Finanzen und geben ihnen die Finanzkennzahlen an die Hand, die sie für die besten Entscheidungen für ihr Unternehmen brauchen.

Gleichzeitig helfen wir Steuerkanzleien, weniger Zeit mit repetitiven Aufgaben und mehr Zeit mit der Beratung ihrer Mandant:innen zu verbringen.

Kontext

Pennylane ist eines der am schnellsten wachsenden Fintechs in Frankreich – und wir sind im zweiten Jahr unserer Expansion nach Deutschland, mit unserem deutschen Team in Berlin.

In 6 Jahren unseres Bestehens haben wir Folgendes erreicht:

  • 💻 Wir haben uns als bahnbrechende Buchhaltungs- und Finanzsoftware für kleine Unternehmen und ihre Steuerberater:innen bekannt gemacht.

Warum ist diese Rolle so wichtig für uns?

Das SDR-Team ist entscheidend dafür, wie wir neue Kund:innen gewinnen.

Als erstes Glied in unserer Sales-Kette prüfen SDRs, welche Anfragen gut zu Pennylane passen, und machen daraus Gesprächstermine – und legen damit die Basis für den Erfolg des gesamten Teams.

Das deutsche SDR-Team besteht aktuell aus 2 Personen, und du gestaltest es mit, während es wächst. Du brauchst keine jahrelange Sales-Erfahrung, um bei uns einzusteigen: Diese Rolle ist als Berufseinstieg im Vertrieb gedacht – wir investieren in dich mit unserer Sales Academy, einem Buddy aus dem Sales-Team und einem klaren Entwicklungsplan.

Wie trägst du zum Projekt bei?

Wir erhalten täglich viele Inbound-Anfragen von Unternehmen, die Pennylane kennenlernen möchten. Genau mit diesen arbeitest du – 100 % Inbound-Vertrieb, Kaltakquise (Outbound) gibt es in dieser Rolle nicht.

Als erste Ansprechperson für unsere zukünftigen Kund:innen verstehst du ihren Bedarf, begeisterst sie für unsere Lösung und vereinbarst eine Demo mit einem Account Executive – der den Deal dann zum Abschluss bringt.

Konkret heißt das:

  • Du reagierst während deiner Arbeitszeit schnell auf neue Anfragen – in der Regel innerhalb weniger Minuten, denn Tempo entscheidet bei Inbound über den Erfolg

  • Du führst strukturierte Erstgespräche (Discovery-Calls) – Unternehmensgröße, aktuelle Buchhaltung, Bedarf, Timing, Entscheider:innen – und erkennst, ob eine Anfrage zum KMU- oder zum Steuerkanzlei-Team gehört

  • Du fasst per Telefon, E-Mail und LinkedIn nach und reaktivierst Leads, die abgetaucht sind oder einen Termin verpasst haben

  • Du übergibst qualifizierte Leads mit einem klaren Briefing an den Account Executive und hältst Salesforce sauber – Lead-Status, Notizen, nächste Schritte

  • Du teilst Erkenntnisse zu Lead-Qualität und -Quellen mit dem Marketing

Dein Erfolg zeigt sich daran, wie viele passende Gesprächstermine du vereinbarst, wie viele davon stattfinden und aus wie vielen konkrete Verkaufschancen entstehen.

Wie sehen deine Aufgaben im Alltag aus?

Deine Verantwortung wächst mit dir – so sieht dein Weg bei uns aus:

Die ersten 3 Monate

  • Onboarding mit Sales Academy, Buddy und Shadowing: Du lernst Pennylane, unser Produkt, die Lead-Typen und unsere Pitches kennen

  • Du führst deine ersten Calls mit Leads aus kleineren Unternehmen

Monat 4 bis 8

  • Du managst deine eigene Inbound-Pipeline in Salesforce und übernimmst zunehmend komplexere Leads

  • Du bringst dich in die Weiterentwicklung unserer Prozesse ein und gibst Kundenfeedback an Produkt, Customer Care und Marketing weiter

Und danach …

  • Mit wachsender Erfahrung übernimmst du zusätzliche Verantwortung: eigene Projekte, die Pflege unserer Wissensdatenbank (Notion) und die Unterstützung neuer Kolleg:innen

Wen wir suchen

Erste Erfahrungen im Inside Sales, Vertriebsinnendienst oder Kundenservice sind willkommen, etwa als Junior Sales Manager, Sales Development Representative (SDR) oder Business Development Representative (BDR). Auch aus Gastronomie, Hotellerie oder Einzelhandel bringst du wertvolle Erfahrung im Umgang mit Menschen mit. Vertriebserfahrung ist keine Voraussetzung.

  • Du interessierst dich dafür, wie Unternehmen funktionieren, und sprichst gern mit Unternehmer:innen

  • Du bist organisiert, arbeitest gern mit Zielen und magst strukturierte Prozesse

  • Du willst lernen, nimmst Feedback gern an und bleibst beim Nachfassen dran – auch wenn es mal nicht sofort klappt

  • Du führst auf Deutsch souverän telefonische Beratungsgespräche und schreibst verständliche geschäftliche E-Mails; auf Englisch (unsere Unternehmenssprache) fühlst du dich sicher

  • Erfahrung mit einem CRM (idealerweise Salesforce) ist ein Plus

Was wir bieten

  • 📄 Unbefristeter Vollzeitvertrag, Start ab sofort

  • 🏢 Hybrides Arbeiten: 2 Tage pro Woche in unserem Berliner Office, die übrigen Tage flexibel

  • 🎓 Strukturiertes Onboarding: Sales Academy, Buddy-Programm und Shadowing

  • 🚀 Entwicklungsperspektive in Richtung Account Executive – abhängig von Leistung und offenen Positionen

  • 🌴 Unabhängig davon, wo du ansässig bist, erhältst du 30 von Pennylane bezahlte Urlaubstage.

  • 💵 Du erhältst ein wettbewerbsfähiges Vergütungspaket.

  • 📈 Du erhältst Unternehmensanteile, um vom Erfolg mitzuprofitieren, den du gemeinsam mit uns aufbaust.

  • 🏡 Du erhältst ein Budget, um dein Zuhause in einen komfortableren Arbeitsplatz zu verwandeln, sowie eine monatliche Pauschale, um in einem Coworking Space zu arbeiten, wann immer du möchtest. In Berlin haben wir ein Office, aus dem regelmäßig gearbeitet werden kann.

  • 🇬🇧 Du erhältst Zugang zu Busuu, um dein Englisch oder Französisch zu perfektionieren.

  • 💻 Du erhältst die neueste Apple-Ausrüstung.

  • 🎉 Wir legen Wert auf regelmäßige gemeinsame Veranstaltungen wie unsere Tech Days (die Remote-Pennylaner alle 3 Monate zusammenbringen) oder unser jährliches Firmenseminar, um wichtige Momente des Zusammenhalts für alle zu schaffen.

🤝 Bewerbungsprozess

  3. Praktische Case Study und Debrief mit Jacob, Global Head of Sales SME, und einem Mitglied des Sales-SME-Teams (45 Min.) – keine Vorbereitung nötig; wir schauen auf Gesprächsführung und Lernfähigkeit, nicht auf Produktwissen

title: Sales Development Representative (SDR) – SME | Berlin (Hybrid)
description:
Sales Development Representative (SDR, m/w/d) – SME | Berlin (Hybrid)

Unbefristet · Vollzeit · Start ab sofort · Berlin, 2 Tage pro Woche im Office

Starte deine Sales-Karriere als SDR bei Pennylane in Berlin. Du sprichst mit Unternehmen, die bereits Interesse an unserer Software gezeigt haben, klärst ihren Bedarf und vereinbarst passende Demo-Termine für unsere Account Executives – ohne Kaltakquise. Mit Sales Academy, Buddy und Shadowing lernst du den SaaS-Vertrieb von Grund auf.

Du willst Arbeit, die etwas bewirkt – an einem Produkt, das bald Millionen von Unternehmer:innen in Europa helfen könnte?

Du arbeitest am besten in einer Kultur, die auf Vertrauen und Eigenverantwortung setzt?

Dann könnte Pennylane genau der richtige Ort für dich sein.

Unsere Vision

Unser Ziel ist es, die beliebteste Finanzmanagement-Software für KMU in Europa zu werden.

Wir befreien Unternehmer:innen von zeitraubenden Aufgaben in Buchhaltung und Finanzen und geben ihnen die Finanzkennzahlen an die Hand, die sie für die besten Entscheidungen für ihr Unternehmen brauchen.

Gleichzeitig helfen wir Steuerkanzleien, weniger Zeit mit repetitiven Aufgaben und mehr Zeit mit der Beratung ihrer Mandant:innen zu verbringen.

Kontext

Pennylane ist eines der am schnellsten wachsenden Fintechs in Frankreich – und wir sind im zweiten Jahr unserer Expansion nach Deutschland, mit unserem deutschen Team in Berlin.

In 6 Jahren unseres Bestehens haben wir Folgendes erreicht:

  • 💻 Wir haben uns als bahnbrechende Buchhaltungs- und Finanzsoftware für kleine Unternehmen und ihre Steuerberater:innen bekannt gemacht.

  • 💰 Wir haben insgesamt 400 Millionen Euro eingesammelt, unter anderem von Sequoia, dem berühmten Fonds aus dem Silicon Valley, der früh in Unternehmen wie Google, Facebook, Airbnb, Stripe, PayPal und viele mehr investiert hat.

  • 👨‍👩‍👧‍👦 Wir sind von 7 Mitbegründern auf mehr als 1.100 zufriedene Pennylaner angewachsen: Wir gelten heute als einer der besten Arbeitsplätze in Frankreich (auch remote), mit einer Bewertung von 4,6/5 auf Glassdoor.

  • 🌍 Wir haben ein internationales Umfeld mit mehr als 25 Nationalitäten aufgebaut, mit einer starken Remote-freundlichen Kultur, in der 30 % der Mitarbeitenden bereits aus allen Teilen Europas arbeiten.

  • 🤝 Wir haben das Vertrauen tausender Kund:innen und Steuerkanzleien gewonnen – mit herausragenden Bewertungen.

  • 🚀 Bereits mehr als 1.300.000 KMU (kleine und mittlere Unternehmen) und über 6.500 Steuerkanzleien nutzen Pennylane in Frankreich!

Warum ist diese Rolle so wichtig für uns?

Das SDR-Team ist entscheidend dafür, wie wir neue Kund:innen gewinnen.

Als erstes Glied in unserer Sales-Kette prüfen SDRs, welche Anfragen gut zu Pennylane passen, und machen daraus Gesprächstermine – und legen damit die Basis für den Erfolg des gesamten Teams.

Das deutsche SDR-Team besteht aktuell aus 2 Personen, und du gestaltest es mit, während es wächst. Du brauchst keine jahrelange Sales-Erfahrung, um bei uns einzusteigen: Diese Rolle ist als Berufseinstieg im Vertrieb gedacht – wir investieren in dich mit unserer Sales Academy, einem Buddy aus dem Sales-Team und einem klaren Entwicklungsplan.

Wie trägst du zum Projekt bei?

Wir erhalten täglich viele Inbound-Anfragen von Unternehmen, die Pennylane kennenlernen möchten. Genau mit diesen arbeitest du – 100 % Inbound-Vertrieb, Kaltakquise (Outbound) gibt es in dieser Rolle nicht.

Als erste Ansprechperson für unsere zukünftigen Kund:innen verstehst du ihren Bedarf, begeisterst sie für unsere Lösung und vereinbarst eine Demo mit einem Account Executive – der den Deal dann zum Abschluss bringt.

Konkret heißt das:

  • Du reagierst während deiner Arbeitszeit schnell auf neue Anfragen – in der Regel innerhalb weniger Minuten, denn Tempo entscheidet bei Inbound über den Erfolg

  • Du führst strukturierte Erstgespräche (Discovery-Calls) – Unternehmensgröße, aktuelle Buchhaltung, Bedarf, Timing, Entscheider:innen – und erkennst, ob eine Anfrage zum KMU- oder zum Steuerkanzlei-Team gehört

  • Du fasst per Telefon, E-Mail und LinkedIn nach und reaktivierst Leads, die abgetaucht sind oder einen Termin verpasst haben

  • Du übergibst qualifizierte Leads mit einem klaren Briefing an den Account Executive und hältst Salesforce sauber – Lead-Status, Notizen, nächste Schritte

  • Du teilst Erkenntnisse zu Lead-Qualität und -Quellen mit dem Marketing

Dein Erfolg zeigt sich daran, wie viele passende Gesprächstermine du vereinbarst, wie viele davon stattfinden und aus wie vielen konkrete Verkaufschancen entstehen.

Wie sehen deine Aufgaben im Alltag aus?

Deine Verantwortung wächst mit dir – so sieht dein Weg bei uns aus:

Die ersten 3 Monate

  • Onboarding mit Sales Academy, Buddy und Shadowing: Du lernst Pennylane, unser Produkt, die Lead-Typen und unsere Pitches kennen

  • Du führst deine ersten Calls mit Leads aus kleineren Unternehmen

Monat 4 bis 8

  • Du managst deine eigene Inbound-Pipeline in Salesforce und übernimmst zunehmend komplexere Leads

  • Du bringst dich in die Weiterentwicklung unserer Prozesse ein und gibst Kundenfeedback an Produkt, Customer Care und Marketing weiter

Und danach …

  • Mit wachsender Erfahrung übernimmst du zusätzliche Verantwortung: eigene Projekte, die Pflege unserer Wissensdatenbank (Notion) und die Unterstützung neuer Kolleg:innen

  • Abhängig von deiner Leistung und offenen Positionen kannst du dich perspektivisch in Richtung Account Executive entwickeln

Wen wir suchen

  • Du möchtest im Vertrieb durchstarten – als Berufseinsteiger:in oder Quereinsteiger:in. Erste Erfahrungen im Inside Sales, Vertriebsinnendienst oder Kundenservice sind willkommen, etwa als Junior Sales Manager, Sales Development Representative (SDR) oder Business Development Representative (BDR). Auch aus Gastronomie, Hotellerie oder Einzelhandel bringst du wertvolle Erfahrung im Umgang mit Menschen mit. Vertriebserfahrung ist keine Voraussetzung.

  • Du interessierst dich dafür, wie Unternehmen funktionieren, und sprichst gern mit Unternehmer:innen

  • Du führst auf Deutsch souverän telefonische Beratungsgespräche und schreibst verständliche geschäftliche E-Mails; auf Englisch (unsere Unternehmenssprache) fühlst du dich sicher

  • Erfahrung mit einem CRM (idealerweise Salesforce) ist ein Plus

Was wir bieten

  • 📄 Unbefristeter Vollzeitvertrag, Start ab sofort

  • 🏢 Hybrides Arbeiten: 2 Tage pro Woche in unserem Berliner Office, die übrigen Tage flexibel

  • 🎓 Strukturiertes Onboarding: Sales Academy, Buddy-Programm und Shadowing

  • 🚀 Entwicklungsperspektive in Richtung Account Executive – abhängig von Leistung und offenen Positionen

  • 🌴 Unabhängig davon, wo du ansässig bist, erhältst du 30 von Pennylane bezahlte Urlaubstage.

  • 💵 Du erhältst ein wettbewerbsfähiges Vergütungspaket.

  • 📈 Du erhältst Unternehmensanteile, um vom Erfolg mitzuprofitieren, den du gemeinsam mit uns aufbaust.

  • 🏡 Du erhältst ein Budget, um dein Zuhause in einen komfortableren Arbeitsplatz zu verwandeln, sowie eine monatliche Pauschale, um in einem Coworking Space zu arbeiten, wann immer du möchtest. In Berlin haben wir ein Office, aus dem regelmäßig gearbeitet werden kann.

  • 🇬🇧 Du erhältst Zugang zu Busuu, um dein Englisch oder Französisch zu perfektionieren.

  • 💻 Du erhältst die neueste Apple-Ausrüstung.

  • 🎉 Wir legen Wert auf regelmäßige gemeinsame Veranstaltungen wie unsere Tech Days (die Remote-Pennylaner alle 3 Monate zusammenbringen) oder unser jährliches Firmenseminar, um wichtige Momente des Zusammenhalts für alle zu schaffen.

title: Senior SAP FICO Consultant (m/f/d)
description:
At Flix, we offer a dynamic work environment with competitive pay, strong growth opportunities, and a tech-driven approach to making travel more accessible, sustainable, and affordable.  

We're looking for an experienced SAP functional Consultant (m/f/d) to join our ERP Finance team at Flix, in Berlin or Munich. 

In the Foundation Division of FlixTech, the ERP Finance team is responsible for the platform that powers our financial backbone: accounting, controlling, procurement, period close, and the integrations that connect them to the rest of Flix. We're setting up a new ERP system for our Train business (FlixTrain) with a first focus on Finance and Procurement. 

As our in-house SAP expert, you'll work closely with our Finance and Procurement teams as well as external partners to make sure the new ERP fits our needs: today and in the long run. After go-live, you'll be the person who owns, evolves and continuously improves the SAP solution from the inside. 

This role is well suited for someone who enjoys ownership, working close to real business problems, and combining solid SAP craftsmanship with a long-term, in-house perspective 

About the Role

  • Act as Flix's in-house SAP expert during the implementation of our new ERP, with a focus on Finance and Procurement. 
  • Translate business requirements from Finance, Procurement and adjacent functions into clean, scalable SAP solutions. 
  • Work closely with external implementation partners during design, build, testing and cut over. 
  • Support data migration, test management, and go-live preparation from a Flix-side ownership perspective. 
  • Take long-term ownership of the SAP solution after go-live: enhancements, change requests, integrations and continuous process improvement. 
  • Contribute to building broader SAP capability within the ERP Finance team thought teaching and mentoring. 
  • Be a trusted advisor to Finance and Procurement stakeholders on what SAP can do for 

About You

  • 7+ years of experience as an SAP Consultant (incl. 5+ years in S/4HANA), with a strong focus on Finance (FI/CO) and Procurement (MM).
  • Hands-on experience with SAP S/4HANA Public Cloud.
  • Additional working knowledge in SAP Supply Chain and Asset Management modules. 
  • At least two full end-to-end SAP implementations, ideally in a company of similar size and complexity to Flix. 
  • Solid understanding of core finance and procurement processes: General Ledger, Accounts Payable / Receivable, Fixed Assets, Controlling, Purchase-to-Pay. 
  • Experience working with external system integrators and the confidence to engage with them as an equal partner. 
  • Comfortable engaging with senior Finance and Procurement stakeholders and translating between business and SAP language. 
  • Structured, pragmatic, delivery-oriented; strong communication and facilitation skills. 
  • Based in Germany, you're fluent in German and English. 

We recognize that everyone carries a unique set of valuable skills and experiences. If you think you could have an impact even though you don't meet 100% of the requirements, we still encourage you to apply. We want to hear from you!  

What We Offer

  • Travel perks: 12 free Flix vouchers + 12 discount vouchers for friends & family. 
  • Work from (M)Anywhere: Depending on your role, work from another location for up to 60 days per year. 
  • Hybrid work model: We are an office-first company, but we offer flexibility to balance work and life. 
  • Wellbeing support: Access confidential 1:1 counselling, courses, and stress management for yourself and up to four family members. 
  • Learning & Development: Take advantage of language classes, training courses, and expert-led sessions to grow your skills. 
  • Mentoring Program: Connect with experienced colleagues to gain insights and accelerate your career. 

To view more local benefits specific to each office location, please check out this link: Locations - Flix Career

Why Join Flix?

At Flix, you'll find teams that rally together to overcome challenges and spark creativity. We believe in ownership culture - giving you the freedom to take initiative, make an impact, and shape your own career path.
As we continue to expand across the globe, you can make a real difference in how we work.

If you're ready to grow and lead your journey, Flix is the place for you!

Senior Product Engineer (DevTools & AI reliability, remote)
description:
(Fully remote, async-first, DevTools SaaS, 32-40h/week, time zones: UTC-3 to UTC+3)

The best developers don't wait for a customer to tell them something's broken.

They catch it first, in the pull request, in staging, or in the checkout flow at 3am, before a single user notices. That instinct is Checkly's whole reason to exist. We give developers and their agents the tools to own reliability the way they own their code: end-to-end tests and synthetic monitoring defined as code, powered by OpenTelemetry and Playwright, versioned and reviewed like everything else they ship. From pull request to post-mortem, in one place.

Thousands of them, from modern AI companies like Mistral and resolve.ai to large engineering orgs like LinkedIn, Citi, and 1Password, build with us. In 2024 we raised $20M in Series B funding from Balderton, CRV and Accel.

Here's the thing about 2026: AI agents and coding assistants are shipping more software, faster, than any team could review by hand, and more of it is breaking in ways nobody has seen before. LLM-backed features fail probabilistically. Agents take actions no runbook anticipated. "Is my app healthy?" is becoming an unanswerable question for a whole generation of AI-native software. You will build reliability for this kind of software.

Our stack is AI (Codex, Claude, use what you like best), Vue.js, TypeScript, Node.js, Golang, Postgres, ClickHouse and AWS. We ship to prod all day, every day. We practice Agile (not scrum) and take pride in good documentation and good looking products.

We’re a remote-first startup that keeps things simple—low on meetings, high on productivity, and always shipping. If you love building cool things, working async, actually listening to and working with customers, and keeping it lean, you’ll fit right in!

What you'll do

Build and ship with AI

You will actively use coding agents for full stack development, from exploring solutions and generating scaffolding to refactoring, test generation and debugging. At Checkly we push the limits of AI tools every day.

Talk to our users

You will talk directly to the developers, DevOps and Site Reliability Engineering (SRE) teams who are on-call, debugging incidents, or wiring Checkly into production pipelines. You will understand their workflows, pain points, and feedback. You use those conversations to validate ideas, course-correct early, and iterate on what you build. Customer calls and the weekly support rotation are part of the job, not a distraction from it.

Find the right problems to solve

In a world where the cost of building software trends to zero, the hard part is picking what to build. You will focus on real developer pain: flaky tests and flaky checks, unclear failures, noisy alerts. You will favour pragmatic solutions that ship quickly, validate assumptions in production, and compound into long-term reliability improvements.

Own your work end to end

From shaping the initial idea, through implementation and rollout, to watching how it behaves in production. You will take part in on-call and help support customers when things don’t work as expected.

title: Talent Partner - Manufacturing and Industrial
description:
Accelerating embodied AGI.

The next ten years of AI will not be won in software. They will be won in the physical world: in factories, hospitals, kitchens, fields, and homes. The companies that own that data will own the century.

microagi is building it. We are a data research and deployment lab. Atlas captures the manual work inside Europe’s industrial champions, trains foundation models on it, and deploys the right robot onto the floor, with no teleoperation and no interruption to the line. Shift records how physical work actually happens and turns it into training-ready data.

We were founded by former Formula 1 engineers from Red Bull Racing and Mercedes, together with a researcher from the Alan Turing Institute. Our $55M seed round, the largest in German history, was led by Hummingbird with Northzone, LocalGlobe, Village Global, and redalpine. We are based in Munich, with our research centre in Zürich and teams in London, New York, and Istanbul. We are now building the engineering and research teams that will take Atlas into new industries.

We're scaling incredibly fast, and our manufacturing capability is central to our future. As our Talent Partner, you'll be focused on hiring workers across the manufacturing lifecycle.

What You Will Do

  • Develop and nurture talent pools across the manufacturing space, such as facilities managers and factory technicians, to ensure consistent delivery across high-volume pipelines.

  • Build a robust employer brand, enabling microagi to be known as a competitive employer in an emerging industrial startup ecosystem.

  • Advise the team on best practices for building out and scaling manufacturing recruiting.

  • Plan and attend industry events to further our market presence amongst the best manufacturing talent.

Requirements

  • 5+ year track record in high-volume blue-collar manufacturing hiring in innovative manufacturing environments

  • Deep network within European manufacturing and industrial talent pools

  • High agency: you don't wait to be told what to do.

  • Fluent in German and English.

Nice to Have

  • Experience working in a fast-paced start-up or scale-up

Who Will Thrive at microagi

Everyone we hire is assessed on the same four traits:

  • Mission and vision: you care about what we are building and why it matters, and your past choices show it.

  • Intensity: you work at a pace that matches the size of the opportunity, and you sustain it.

  • Entrepreneurial: you start things nobody asked for, and you finish them.

  • Raw IQ: you learn fast, reason from first principles, and get sharper when the problem changes.

This is for you if:

  • You would rather own a problem end to end than wait for a spec.

  • You use AI every day, and you can tell a correct answer from a plausible one.

  • You want to work in person, in the office, with people who are very good at what they do.

This is not for you if:

  • You are looking for a predictable 9-to-5.

  • You would forward output you cannot explain.

  • "That’s not my job" feels like a reasonable answer.

How We Hire

We read every application and reply within five working days.

  1. Talent Screen (30 min): a first conversation, both ways.

  2. Technical or Functional Interview (60 min): how you think when the problem changes.

  3. Your Work (60 min): bring something you are proud of and walk us through it.

  4. Leadership (30 min): a conversation with our CEO.

  5. Coworking Day (engineering and research roles): a day building with the team on a real problem.

Then a decision, usually within a few days.

Pay Transparency

Compensation includes base salary and equity. The salary range for this role is shown on this posting.

What We Offer

  • Agency: real ownership from day one, and decisions that actually matter.

  • Freedom: to choose how you solve the problem, without layers of approval.

  • A seat on a rocketship: one of Europe’s fastest-growing deep-tech companies, at the earliest stage.

  • Free food and drinks in the office.

Equal Opportunity

• Co-founder/CFO @SoftOne (exited)

Your Role

More than 50 million people already use EverAI’s products, and we’re growing toward 100 million.

The audience is already here. The opportunity is what happens next.

We’re hiring a Senior Lifecycle Marketing Manager to take CRM to an entirely new level. Your mission is clear: turn it into a major revenue channel by converting more users, increasing repeat purchases, and giving people compelling reasons to keep coming back.

You’ll own everything within CRM, from onboarding and first purchase to retention and reactivation, across email, push notifications, in-product messaging, and promotions.

You’ll report directly to Thomas Lacroix, our Co-founder and CMO, with the freedom to rethink journeys, test ambitious ideas, and build the CRM playbook that gets us there.

At our scale, even small improvements can influence millions of user journeys and create significant growth.

If you’re looking for more than a campaign-management role, this is your opportunity to drive measurable growth at exceptional scale.

  • Own one of EverAI’s biggest growth opportunities: lead the strategy and execution across the full CRM lifecycle, from onboarding and conversion through repeat purchasing, retention, and reactivation

  • Find the growth hiding in our user base: use behavioral data to uncover where users lose interest, stop engaging, or miss an opportunity to purchase

  • Crack the first-purchase challenge: create onboarding, abandoned-payment, offer, and follow-up journeys that turn more registered users into paying customers

  • Keep users coming back: increase token purchases, repeat purchasing, retention, reactivation, and LTV through smarter segmentation, personalization, and timing

  • Test big ideas quickly: build experiments, measure what genuinely moved the numbers, scale the winners, and turn each result into the next opportunity

title: Senior Partner Manager (German speaking)
description:
About Us

Perk (formerly TravelPerk) is the intelligent platform for travel and spend management. Built to tackle the time-consuming, manual work that gets in the way of real work, our tools automate everything from travel bookings to expenses, invoice processing, and more.
