title: Frontend Engineer
description:
About ActAI

There are over 5 billion users using basic applications today such email, notes, tasks, calendar and they're not AI-native. Our mission is to build proactive applications for anyone in the world, who are not used to complex prompting. We aim to bring intelligence to conversations, errands, organising and workflows, with minimal to no prompting.

Our first application is an agent-first mobile communication app. We believe building applications that users use daily for communication, coordination and collaboration needs will help integrate AI into their lives. The net effect is to eliminate misinformation, achieve low coordination costs, enable high quality tasks and collaboration at scale with minimal or little prompting.

 

Role

As a Web Frontend Engineer, you will build the core web experiences, including Chat, Notes, Calendar, Docs and Sheets.

You will own complex, highly interactive product surfaces from architecture through implementation, working closely with product, design, backend and AI engineers to make AI a native part of how users communicate, write, organise and work.

 

What You'll Own

  • Build major web experiences across Chat, Notes, Calendar, Docs, and Sheets.

  • Develop complex interactions including real-time messaging, collaborative editing, rich-text editing, scheduling, tables, and spreadsheets.

  • Build reusable frontend architecture and components that work consistently across ActAI applications.

  • Integrate streaming AI responses, proactive actions, and model-driven experiences directly into product workflows.

  • Own frontend performance, responsiveness, reliability and accessibility across browsers and devices.

  • Work closely with product and design to take ideas from prototype to production quickly.

 

What We're Looking For

  • Strong experience building complex, production web applications using React, TypeScript and modern frontend technologies.

  • Deep understanding of frontend architecture, state management, browser APIs, and performance.

  • Experience building highly interactive products such as chat, collaboration, productivity, document editing, calendars, or workspaces.

  • Experience with real-time systems, WebSockets, streaming APIs, or collaborative interfaces.

  • Strong product and UI judgment with attention to interaction details.

  • Able to independently own features from technical design through production.

 

Outcomes

  • Users can communicate, write, organise and collaborate seamlessly across Chat, Notes, Calendar, Docs and Sheets.

  • Complex interactions such as group messaging, editing, scheduling and collaboration feel fast and reliable.

  • AI capabilities are integrated naturally into product workflows rather than added as separate chatbot experiences.

  • Frontend architecture remains fast, maintainable and reusable as ActAI expands into new applications and workflows.

 

Tech Stack

  • TypeScript

  • React.js / Next.js

  • HTML / CSS

  • WebSockets / streaming APIs

  • Node.js

  • REST / GraphQL APIs

 

How We Work

The best products today in the world were built by small, world-class teams. We are a high talent density and hands-on team. We make decisions collectively and move at rapid speed, striking a balance between shipping high-quality work and learning.

Joining our team requires the ability to bring structure, exercise judgment and execute independently. Our goal is to put in the hands of our users a truly magical product.

 

Interview Process

If there appears to be a fit, we'll reach out to schedule 3, but no more than 4 interviews.

Applications are evaluated by our technical team members. Interviews will be conducted via virtual meetings and/or onsite.

We value transparency and efficiency, so expect a prompt decision. If you've demonstrated the exceptional skills and mindset we're looking for, we'll extend an offer to join us and help bring practical AI benefits to billions of users globally.

title: Forward Deployed Engineer
description:
About SANOVIO

SANOVIO makes buying and selling medical supplies easier. On our AI platform, hospitals, purchasing groups and suppliers work together in one place instead of juggling emails, Excel lists and disconnected systems. Hospitals can buy together, and suppliers reach that bundled demand more easily.

Our software, SANOVIO aOS, uses AI agents to take over the tedious work: cleaning up product data, comparing requests and offers, bundling demand and keeping orders on track. It connects to the systems our customers already use.

When needed, SANOVIO Fulfillment also takes care of the physical side: finding manufacturers worldwide, quality checks, financing, warehousing and delivery. The goal is simple: less admin work, and more time and money for patient care.

About the Role

As a Forward Deployed Engineer, you are the bridge between our customers and our product, on both sides of the platform: healthcare providers and purchasing groups on one side, suppliers on the other. At its core, this role is about talking to customers. You work directly with procurement, logistics and IT teams, understand how they really work and make SANOVIO work inside their world: you connect our platform to their ERP, materials management and supplier systems, untangle their data and processes, and ship the solutions that make them successful.

This role is for builders who are just as comfortable in a customer workshop as in a code editor. Whether you studied business informatics, industrial engineering, computer science or mathematics, or bring experience in technical product management, product engineering or software engineering with a strong design sense: what matters is that you love solving messy real-world problems end to end. We hire for skills, not for degrees.

Tasks

  • Talking to our customers every day: leading workshops with procurement managers, IT departments and suppliers, and being a trusted partner for our customers

  • Owning customer implementations end to end, from kickoff and process analysis to go-live and continuous improvement

  • Analyzing and redesigning procurement processes on both sides, from requisition and ordering at healthcare providers to order handling at suppliers, and uncovering optimization potential

  • Designing, building and running integrations between SANOVIO and our customers' ERP systems (such as SAP), materials management and supplier systems

  • Onboarding and harmonizing customer data (e.g. article master data, catalogs, order histories) and building robust data pipelines and mappings

  • Configuring and extending our AI agents for customer-specific workflows such as data matching and order automation

  • Prototyping and shipping customer-facing workflows, tools and dashboards with a strong focus on usability for non-technical users

  • Bringing customer insights back into the product and turning recurring solutions into product features together with our engineering team and the founders

Communication and customer focus

  • You enjoy talking to customers: you listen carefully, ask the right questions and explain technical topics in plain language

  • Native-level German and very good English, so you can confidently lead conversations and workshops with our customers

  • Confident with all kinds of stakeholders, from procurement managers to IT departments

  • Willing to work on-site in Munich and to travel regularly to customers in Germany and Switzerland

General Profile

  • Degree in Business Informatics (Wirtschaftsinformatik), Industrial Engineering (Wirtschaftsingenieurwesen), Computer Science, Mathematics or a similar field. Skills matter more to us than your degree, so equivalent hands-on experience counts just as much

  • Strong process understanding: you enjoy mapping, analyzing and improving business processes such as procure-to-pay or supply chain

  • High ownership, structured problem-solving and the drive to deliver fast in ambiguous environments

  • This is a junior role: a great fit if you're a recent graduate or have up to five years of professional experience. Internships and working student jobs count too

Technical skillset

  • First hands-on experience with system integrations and interfaces (e.g. REST APIs, webhooks, EDI or file-based interfaces), whether from work, internships or university projects

Here at The Exploration Company, we are building spacecrafts for humanity.

[Deutsche Version weiter unten]

Your Mission

At The Exploration Company, we develop, manufacture, and operate Nyx — a modular, reusable orbital spacecraft designed to be refuelled in orbit and transport cargo, with crewed missions potentially planned for the longer term.

We’re looking for a hands-on, technically mature professional with an engineering degree or extensive CNC experience to take full ownership of the machining process for space-grade components. You’ll be responsible for CAM programming, machine setup and optimisation, and continuous improvement. You’ll also contribute directly to future investments in machining equipment and tooling.

You’ll work on a variety of high-precision parts, including rocket engine components, post-processed metal 3D-printed parts, and critical propulsion subcomponents. You’ll work across a fleet of modern, multi-brand, 5-axis machining centres and CNC lathes.

This role offers a high-impact technical position, with opportunities for career growth and increased responsibility.

Fluency in English is expected, as our work environment is international.

Your Responsibilities

  • Define and optimise machining strategies, including sequencing, tooling, fixtures, and in-process controls.

  • Program complex components in HyperMill or equivalent CAM software for 5-axis milling and CNC turning.

  • Validate parts using multi-brand CNC equipment, ensuring that they meet tolerance and surface-finish requirements.

  • Manufacture rocket engine components, precision assemblies, propulsion subcomponents, and Inconel structures, including setting workpiece origins and preparing cutting tools.

  • Perform first-line maintenance to keep machines in good working order.

  • Analyse and improve toolpaths, reduce cycle times, and stabilise machining quality.

  • Work with design, quality, and production teams to provide feedback, propose design improvements, and troubleshoot issues.

  • Lead equipment investment efforts, including specification development, supplier coordination, and commissioning.

Profile

  • An engineering degree or 5+ years of experience as a highly skilled technician in CNC/CAM machining of complex parts.

  • Expertise in HyperMill or equivalent CAM software and tight-tolerance machining.

  • Solid knowledge of 5-axis milling and/or precision turning.

  • Experience working with space or aerospace materials, such as Inconel, titanium, and other high-performance alloys.

  • An autonomous, hands-on approach, with the ability to structure and lead technical topics.

  • An interest in developing machining capabilities through process and equipment leadership.


Deutsche Version

Deine Mission

Bei The Exploration Company entwickeln, fertigen und betreiben wir Nyx – ein modulares, wiederverwendbares Orbitalfahrzeug, das im All betankt werden und Fracht transportieren kann. Langfristig sind auch bemannte Missionen vorgesehen.

Wir suchen eine praxisorientierte, technisch versierte Persönlichkeit mit einem Ingenieurabschluss oder umfangreicher CNC-Erfahrung, die den gesamten Bearbeitungsprozess für weltraumtaugliche Komponenten eigenverantwortlich übernimmt. Du bist für die CAM-Programmierung, das Einrichten und Optimieren der Maschinen sowie die kontinuierliche Prozessverbesserung verantwortlich. Darüber hinaus wirkst du direkt an zukünftigen Investitionen in Bearbeitungstechnik und Werkzeuge mit.

Du arbeitest an unterschiedlichsten hochpräzisen Bauteilen – darunter Komponenten für Raketentriebwerke, nachbearbeitete Metall-3D-Druckteile und kritische Subkomponenten von Antriebssystemen. Dabei nutzt du einen modernen Maschinenpark mit 5-Achs-Bearbeitungszentren und CNC-Drehmaschinen verschiedener Hersteller.

Diese Position bietet dir eine technisch anspruchsvolle Aufgabe mit hoher Wirkung sowie die Möglichkeit, künftig zusätzliche Verantwortung zu übernehmen und dich weiterzuentwickeln.

Sehr gute Englischkenntnisse werden vorausgesetzt, da unser Arbeitsumfeld international geprägt ist.

Deine Aufgaben

  • Bearbeitungsstrategien definieren und optimieren, einschließlich Bearbeitungsreihenfolge, Werkzeugauswahl, Vorrichtungen und prozessbegleitender Qualitätskontrolle

  • Komplexe Bauteile in HyperMill (oder ähnlicher Software) programmieren, einschließlich 5-Achs-Fräsen und CNC-Drehen

  • Bauteile auf CNC-Maschinen verschiedener Hersteller validieren und dabei Maßhaltigkeit sowie Oberflächenqualität sicherstellen

  • Raketentriebwerkskomponenten, präzise Subkomponenten von Antriebssystemen und Inconel-Strukturen fertigen, einschließlich der Einrichtung von Werkstücknullpunkten und der Vorbereitung der Schneidwerkzeuge

  • Erstwartungs- und Instandhaltungsarbeiten durchführen, um die Maschinen in einwandfreiem Zustand zu halten

  • Werkzeugwege analysieren und verbessern, Bearbeitungszeiten reduzieren und eine stabile Bearbeitungsqualität sicherstellen

  • Mit den Teams aus Konstruktion, Qualitätssicherung und Produktion zusammenarbeiten, um Feedback zu geben, Konstruktionsvorschläge einzubringen und technische Probleme zu lösen

  • Investitionsprojekte für Maschinen und Anlagen vorantreiben – von der Spezifikation über die Koordination mit Lieferanten bis hin zur Inbetriebnahme

Dein Profil

  • Abgeschlossenes Ingenieurstudium oder mindestens fünf Jahre Berufserfahrung als hochqualifizierter Techniker im Bereich CNC/CAM für komplexe Bauteile

  • Fundierte Erfahrung mit HyperMill oder vergleichbaren CAM-Systemen sowie in der Bearbeitung mit engen Toleranzen

  • Sehr gute Kenntnisse im 5-Achs-Fräsen und/oder Präzisionsdrehen

  • Erfahrung mit Werkstoffen aus der Raumfahrt- bzw. Luft- und Raumfahrtindustrie, insbesondere Inconel, Titan und Hochleistungslegierungen

  • Selbstständige und praxisorientierte Arbeitsweise sowie die Fähigkeit, technische Themen zu strukturieren und voranzutreiben

  • Interesse daran, den Ausbau unserer Fertigungskompetenzen durch die Weiterentwicklung von Prozessen und Anlagen aktiv mitzugestalten

Warum The Exploration Company?

  • Eine ganzheitliche Aufgabe – von der Vorbereitung bis zur Auslieferung – mit hoher Eigenverantwortung

  • Direkte Mitwirkung an der Fertigung von Raumfahrtkomponenten der nächsten Generation

  • Die Möglichkeit, eine moderne Fertigungswerkstatt mit aufzubauen und zukünftige Industrieinvestitionen zu verantworten

  • Klare Entwicklungsperspektiven in Richtung technische Leitung oder Management innerhalb eines schnell wachsenden Unternehmens

  • Ein multikulturelles, internationales Team, das sich leidenschaftlich für die Erforschung des Weltraums begeistert

The Exploration Company ist ein Arbeitgeber, der Chancengleichheit fördert und sich der Vielfalt verpflichtet.

  • Wir diskriminieren niemanden aufgrund von ethnischer Herkunft, Religion, Hautfarbe, nationaler Herkunft, Geschlecht, sexueller Orientierung, Alter, Familienstand oder Behinderung.

  • Unterstützung beim Umzug, einschließlich Visa-Unterstützung bei Bedarf, ist verfügbar.

Why you should join us!

What makes us special here at The Exploration Company and why we think you will enjoy working here is:  

  • We’re Agile - we make decisions fast whilst keeping our goals and systems in mind 

  • We’re Open and Collaborative - we are transparent about risks and obstacles, so that we can cooperate to overcome them  

  • We have a lot of Fun - we refuel our energy knowing we are democratising space. It’s a wonderful and rare opportunity, are YOU up for the challenge?  

We'd love to hear from you if you wish to be a part of our journey. Please submit your CV now for immediate consideration and we will be in touch shortly.

title: System Engineer (ISOS Host)

Our Future Projects unit is dedicated to expanding and complementing these capabilities by conceptualizing and pre-developing new technologies, products and programs.

title: Senior Export Control Manager - Defense (m/f/d)
description:
TYTAN Technologies

The PACE is fast. The expectations are high. The contribution matters. Working at TYTAN is more than a job, this is a mission. We push boundaries, think big, and hold ourselves to the highest standard. Our mission and values guide everything we do, and we're looking for people who are driven by ownership, embrace challenges, and are energized by meaningful work. If you're motivated by impact and thrive in dynamic environments, you'll fit right in.

At TYTAN, we aim to set a global standard in autonomous air defense with AI-driven, cost-efficient systems that counter unmanned aerial threats at scale. We protect people. We protect critical infrastructure. We protect European sovereignty.

We are looking for an Senior Export Control Manager whose has understanding of defense product related export control and customs regulation to ensure full compliance with export control, customs, and trade regulations across our operations.

The role works closely with Logistics, Procurement, Production, and Engineering, while owning all export control and customs compliance topics within the Operations team, specifically related to the production and international movement of KWL-controlled goods.

You will act as the subject matter expert for both export control and customs, ensuring compliant classification, licensing, customs processes, and documentation across the entire operational value chain.

Your Roadmap to Make an Impact

Export Control & Trade Compliance

  • Ensure compliance with German, EU, and international export control regulations, including AWG, AWV, EU Dual-Use Regulation, and applicable international regimes.

  • Own export control topics for KWL-controlled goods, including classification, licensing, documentation, and audit readiness.

  • Classify products, components, software, and technology (e.g. KWL, ECCN, HS) in cooperation with Engineering and Product Management.

  • Determine licensing requirements, apply for and manage export licenses, and conduct embargo, sanctions, and restricted party screenings.

Customs & Import / Export Operations

  • Ensure compliance with customs regulations for imports and exports, including tariff classification (HS), customs valuation, origin determination, and preference management.

  • Coordinate customs processes with freight forwarders, customs brokers, and authorities.

  • Review and approve customs documentations and manage customs-related authorizations and procedures (e.g. simplified procedures, AEO where applicable).

Operations & Supply Chain Collaboration

  • Work closely with Logistics, Production Planning and Procurement to ensure compliant material flow.

  • Advise Operations on compliance implications for manufacturing, internal transfers, re-exports, and technology access.

  • Support onboarding of new suppliers and logistics partners and ensure export control and customs requirements are embedded into operational workflows and ERP systems.

  • Support item onboarding to ensure data quality across the product life-cycle.

Process Ownership & Governance

  • Develop, implement, and continuously improve export control and customs processes, SOPs, and work instructions within Operations.

  • Maintain complete and audit-ready documentation, records, and prepare and support internal and external audits, and authority requests.

  • Act as the main point of contact for export control and customs authorities and external advisors.

Leadership & Advisory

  • Act as a lead for export control and customs department. Train and advise employees in Operations, Supply Chain, and Logistics on export control and customs requirements.

  • Monitor regulatory changes and assess their impact on different processes and act as escalation point and decision-maker for complex compliance cases.


  • 6+ years of experience in defense product export control, customs, or trade compliance in the defense area.

  • Strong knowledge of German export control regulations (AWG, AWV, KWL) and customs law; EU Dual-Use Regulation required, understanding of US EAR/ITAR is also important .

  • Understanding of export control and customs rules for defense product is a must have.

  • Experience with KWL-controlled goods and complex international supply chains.

  • Hands-on experience with customs classification, valuation, origin, and broker coordination.

  • High level of ownership, structured working style, and attention to detail.

  • Strong stakeholder management and communication skills.

  • Fluency in German and English (written and spoken).

Why TYTAN?

  • Build technology with real operational impact: Develop autonomous defense systems designed to protect lives and strengthen Europe’s security

  • Shape scalable defense capabilities: Work on solutions built for mass deployment, cost efficiency, resilience, and reliable production at scale

  • Contribute to networked air defense: Help integrate our systems into multi-layered defense architectures alongside sensors, command systems, and effectors

  • Develop for real-world operations: Build capabilities together with end users and improve them continuously based on direct operational feedback

  • Move fast and take ownership: Work in a focused, high-performance team where decisions are made quickly and individual contributions have immediate impact

  • Define a new generation of defense technology: Join early and help shape the products, engineering standards, culture, and direction of a fast-growing deep-tech company

  • Work with an international mission-driven team: Collaborate with experienced specialists united by the goal of creating sovereign and effective security capabilities for Europe

Our Benefits

  • Virtual stock options: Participate in our success through virtual stock options (VSOPs) at the company's current valuation

  • Monthly allowances: €106/month in flexible benefits including lunch discounts and EGYM Wellpass or shopping credit

  • Regular health care events: Health check-ups, skin screenings, mental health workshops, and an annual vitamin infusion on us

  • Referral bonus: Earn a reward when someone you refer joins the team

  • Regular team events: On- and off-site activities to connect and celebrate together

  • Corporate discounts: Exclusive employee discounts across a wide range of partner brands

  • Flexibility: Flexible working hours and hybrid work model, plus a modern Munich office built for focus and collaboration

About us

At TYTAN, it is more than just a job; it is about embracing autonomy, personal growth, and purpose. Make a lasting impact in the new era of defense! Join us to create a safer world for all.

Please note that we currently do not offer visa sponsorship, so we’re only able to consider candidates who already have a valid work permit. All qualified applicants are hereby encouraged to apply.

  • Prendre du recul sur les bugs et les potentiels d’amélioration de ton projet pour apprendre de tes erreurs et améliorer le fonctionnement de ton équipe.
Tu vas apprendre à produire un code de qualité 3 à 5 fois plus vite avec l'IA grâce à notre partenariat avec Anthropic ! 
 
Toute la dynamique de l’entreprise repose sur l’engagement des Theodoers dans un apprentissage permanent.
C’est pour cette raison que ton quotidien ne se limite pas aux projets clients : chaque Theodoer contribue à rendre l’entreprise meilleure en développant de nouvelles connaissances pour tous, qu’il partage via des conférences en interne et en externe, des articles de blog, des groupes d’expertises avec d’autres passionnés au sein de Theodo France…
 
Exemple de projets :

Notre ambition est de former les leaders de la tech de demain. Grâce au coaching et formations que l’on propose, tu pourras :

Applied Intuition, Inc. is powering the future of physical AI. Founded in 2017 and now valued at $15 billion, the Silicon Valley company is creating the digital infrastructure needed to bring intelligence to every moving machine on the planet. Applied Intuition services the automotive, defense, trucking, construction, mining and agriculture industries in three core areas: tools and infrastructure, operating systems, and autonomy. Eighteen of the top 20 global automakers, as well as the United States military and its allies, trust the company’s solutions to deliver physical intelligence. Applied Intuition is headquartered in Sunnyvale, California, with offices in Washington, D.C.; San Diego; Ft. Walton Beach, Florida; Ann Arbor, Michigan; London; Stuttgart; Munich; Stockholm; Bangalore; Seoul; and Tokyo. Learn more at applied.co.

We are an in-office company, and our expectation is that full-time employees primarily work from their Applied Intuition office 5 days a week. However, we also recognize the importance of flexibility and trust our employees to manage their schedules responsibly. This may include occasional remote work, starting the day with morning meetings from home before heading to the office, or leaving earlier when needed to accommodate family commitments. This in-office expectation does not apply to contractor positions

About the role

We are looking for a bright engineer to help our customers solve complex technical problems across Applied Intuition’s Vehicle OS portfolio. In this role you will work closely with vehicle software and tooling teams at OEMs and Tier 1s to ensure Applied’s solutions deliver maximum impact in advancing customers’ Software-Defined-Vehicle (SDV) strategies and in-cabin user experiences.

Vehicle OS is Applied Intuition’s software platform for SDV. It enables OEMs to modernize their E/E architecture through three interconnected areas:

  • Middleware & architecture Service-oriented, middleware-driven software stacks built on AUTOSAR Adaptive Platform, SOME/IP, and DDS. Helps OEMs migrate from distributed ECU architectures to zonal, centralized compute.

  • Developer toolchain A code-first toolchain that replaces GUI-bound configuration workflows. Engineers model vehicle behavior in Python, manage changes through pull requests, and validate in virtual ECU environments analogous to what cloud virtual engineering workbenches (e.g., AWS VEW) brought to cloud-native development, but purpose-built for automotive E/E systems.

  • IVI & in-vehicle infotainment Android Automotive OS (AAOS) based platform, HMI/cluster software, and intelligent in-cabin experiences including Cabin Intelligence (DMS, OMS, voice, occupant interaction).

This role sits at the intersection of all three areas, and the balance will depend on the customer mix.

At Applied Intuition, you will:

  • Act as the technical bridge between automotive customers and Applied Intuition’s engineering and product teams

  • Support OEMs in adopting Vehicle OS: middleware stack, developer SDK, and IVI/infotainment integration

Wir wissen: Nicht jede/jeder erfüllt alles und das ist völlig in Ordnung. Bewirb dich, wenn ein Großteil auf dich zutrifft:

  • Eine abgeschlossene kaufmännische Ausbildung oder ein vergleichbares Studium
  • Berufserfahrung passend zu deiner Karrierestufe, von ersten praktischen Erfahrungen (Junior) über mehrjährige Buchhaltungspraxis bis hin zu 3 bis 5+ Jahren und fundierter Bilanzbuchhaltungserfahrung (Senior/Bilanzbuchhalter)
  • Idealerweise (für erfahrene Profile) Praxis aus einer Steuerkanzlei/einem Steuerbüro sowie Beteiligung an oder eigenständige Erstellung von Jahresabschlüssen
  • Kenntnisse in HGB und Finanzbuchhaltung, je nach Level Grundkenntnisse oder umfassende Expertise
  • Begeisterung für digitale Innovationen und Erfahrung bzw. Offenheit im Umgang mit digitalen Workflows
  • Kenntnisse in Microsoft M365 und DATEV (Grundkenntnisse wünschenswert bis sicherer Umgang); Erfahrung mit Business Central, Oracle oder branchenspezifischen ERP-Systemen von Vorteil
  • Ausgeprägtes Zahlenverständnis, Sorgfalt und Genauigkeit
  • Eine selbstständige, lösungsorientierte Arbeitsweise sowie Kommunikationsstärke und Teamfähigkeit, digital wie persönlich
  • Von Vorteil (kein Muss): ein eigenes Mandanten-Netzwerk, das du mit einbringen möchtest

Was wir dir bieten

  • Gestaltungsspielraum: Bring deine Ideen ein und gestalte aktiv die Zukunft der Buchhaltung mit
  • Verantwortung & Entwicklung: Baue unser Team in Düsseldorf mit auf, mit echtem Raum für deine persönliche und fachliche Weiterentwicklung
  • Kontinuierliche Weiterbildung: Bleib am Puls der digitalen Entwicklung, insbesondere bei Workflows und Automatisierung
  • Flexibles Arbeiten: Remote oder im modernen Büro mit höhenverstellbaren Schreibtischen in der Düsseldorfer Altstadt, du hast die Wahl
  • Work-Life-Balance: 30 Urlaubstage, zusätzlich frei an Heiligabend und Silvester sowie flexible Arbeitszeiten
  • Mitarbeiter-Benefits: spendit-Karte, kostenlose Getränke, regelmäßige Teamevents (in Planung)
  • Mobilität: Fahrtkostenzuschuss für das Deutschlandticket und JobRad-Leasing

Über uns

Die advacc advanced accounting GmbH ist der Partner für moderne, vollständig digitale Buchhaltung mit Standorten in Düsseldorf und Greifswald. Als externe Buchhaltung übernehmen wir für unsere Kundinnen und Kunden zentrale Aufgaben der Finanzbuchhaltung, von der Bearbeitung von Ein- und Ausgangsrechnungen über die Buchung aller Geschäftsvorfälle bis zur Lohnabrechnung und stellen fristgerechte, transparente und rechtssichere Abläufe sicher.
Darüber hinaus beraten wir betriebswirtschaftlich, steuern das Forderungsmanagement und treiben die Digitalisierung sowie Optimierung von Buchhaltungsprozessen voran. Unser erfahrenes Team arbeitet softwareunabhängig, schnell und proaktiv, mit dem Anspruch, Abläufe zu vereinfachen, Liquidität zu sichern und Freiräume für das Kerngeschäft unserer Kundinnen und Kunden zu schaffen. Wir stehen für innovative Lösungen, hohe Serviceorientierung und echte Hands-on-Mentalität.

description:
About us

At GotPhoto, we are freeing photographers to be more successful.

Through our platforms GotPhoto.com and fotograf.de, we help professional photographers simplify and transform the way they work — from photo management and client communication to ordering and payment processing. Our end-to-end workflow and e-commerce solution gives photographers more time to focus on what matters most: being behind the lens.

Since 2012, we’ve built a sustainable and profitable business driven by entrepreneurial spirit, innovation, and a deep understanding of photographers’ everyday challenges. Today, thousands of photographers trust our software , creating their own success stories along the way.

As the leading e-commerce engine for professional volume photographers and a business backed by EQT, one of the world’s leading private equity firms, we’re powered by a team of 150+ talented and international people building technology that simplifies photographers’ everyday work and helps them focus on capturing meaningful moments.

Join us on our journey to empower photographers like never before.

Your Role

Do you want to drive turn everyday People administration into a seamless, high-quality experience for every single employee?

Are you ready to support both the operational engine and the talent growth of a fast-paced tech scale-up?

If you are a detail-oriented student who loves supporting people and keeping processes sharp by bringing employees and business needs together, then you are our perfect match!

Expect a steep learning curve, with experienced colleagues by your side. You will gain deep in-depth knowledge of the entire employee life cycle, from initial recruitment to the final stage of a successful career.

What You’ll Do

  • Support People Admin: You help our People Operations with everyday employee inquiries, such as holidays, workations and learning budgets, and you keep our Jira Service Management tickets moving with speed and care.

  • Help Keep Data Accurate: You support the maintenance of employee master data and digital personal files, following clear guidelines, so that everything stays accurate and up to date.

  • Document Support: You prepare employment certificates, reference letters and other essential HR documents in German and English.

  • Talent Spotlight: You help us look after the perfect candidate, from the first review of applications for junior roles to taking notes in interviews, so that the experience stays world-class.

  • Process Coordination: You help the recruiting process run smoothly by scheduling interviews and following up with stakeholders to keep the momentum high.

What You’ll Bring

Experience

  • You are currently enrolled and studying Business Administration, Human Resources Management, Psychology, or a related subject.

  • Initial experience in fast-paced companies or HR environment is a plus.

  • Experience in a Tech Scale-up environment is a bonus.

Skills

  • Bilingual Proficiency: You speak and write German and English at a professional level (C1/Native).

  • Organizational Talent: You can juggle multiple tasks and projects without losing your cool or your attention to detail.

  • Tech Savvy: You are comfortable (or eager to learn) working with tools like Personio, Leapsome, Jira, and Google Workspace.

Mindset

  • Detail Lover: Accuracy is your quiet superpower.

  • Discreet & Trustworthy: You handle sensitive data with care.

  • Eager Learner: You see feedback as fuel.

  • You enjoy both working as part of the People Team and collaborating with it: You come to our Berlin-Mitte office at least twice a week to work alongside us.

Why You’ll Love Life at GotPhoto

  • Best of Both Worlds: We live and breathe a flexible hybrid model. Our beautiful office at Hausvogteiplatz is our vibrant Berlin hub for collaboration, but you have the freedom to leverage the setup that works best for you.

  • Work from (Almost) Anywhere: We believe in flexibility that respects your lifestyle. Once you have completed your probation, you have the option to work remotely from within Europe for up to 40 days per year. Whether you are visiting family or simply seeking a change of scenery, we support a work-from-anywhere culture that helps you stay inspired.

  • Recharge & Unwind: We value your downtime. You start with 26 days of leave, plus we love to top that up with additional discretionary "X-days" to make sure you’re truly rested.

  • Multicultural & Inclusive Team: We thrive on diverse perspectives. Our international team fosters a culture of mutual respect and professional exchange, ensuring that fresh ideas and tolerance are at the heart of everything we build together.

  • Fuel Your Growth: We’re big on learning. You’ll get a dedicated education budget to explore new ideas and grow professionally.

  • Exclusive Employee Discounts: Get more for your money with access to the "Benefits at Work" platform, offering significant discounts on top global brands.

  • Collaborate with software engineers to improve the effectiveness and reliability of our security tooling

  • Interest in vulnerability assessment, penetration testing, and DevSecOps practices

  • Curiosity about security tools, automation, and emerging technologies

  • Ability to work independently while actively collaborating with a development team

title: Senior Backend Engineer, Platform (f/m/d)
description:
Join Apaleo and shape the future of hospitality tech

Apaleo is the world's most open, API-first property management platform, powering the next generation of hospitality operations. Our modular, AI-powered infrastructure lets hoteliers customise their tech stack, automate routine work and deliver seamless, personalised guest experiences, powered by best-in-class apps and autonomous AI agents that adapt to every stay.

If you're driven by the idea of making hospitality smarter, more human and powered by cutting-edge technology, we'd love to hear from you.

About the role

You'll join our Platform team as an individual contributor, working directly with our Platform Lead, who sets Platform's technical direction. Platform owns infrastructure, developer experience and security foundations for the whole engineering organisation. It's a small team, so you'll cover a wide surface area, with no dedicated DevOps or QA function to hand work to.

This is a high-ownership seat. You'll take on substantial, ambiguous, cross-cutting initiatives, agree the direction with the Platform Lead, then drive them from first analysis through to completion with real autonomy over how you get there.

We don't run a groomed backlog or sprint planning. We assign a significant topic to someone who owns it end to end. If you thrive with structure handed to you, this isn't the role. If you love spotting the problem worth solving and driving it yourself, you'll fit right in.

 

What you'll be up to 

  • Designing and building scalable, reliable and maintainable backend systems.
  • Spotting and scoping problems and initiatives yourself, not just picking up assigned tickets: weighing impact, priority and timing.
  • Contributing to architectural decisions and design discussions, and bringing other teams along.
  • Driving substantial, cross-cutting initiatives end to end, coordinating with stakeholders across engineering.
  • Building and maintaining internal tools and infrastructure (AWS, Terraform) that help teams deliver faster and more reliably.
  • Owning observability, logging and operational excellence to keep the platform highly available.
  • Sharing knowledge through code reviews, design reviews and pairing, and helping raise technical standards.
  • Spotting where AI and automation can improve how we build and run software.

 

Some of the challenges waiting for you 

You'll take ownership of one of these as your first initiative, with no other distractions.

  • Solving horizontal write-scaling for our database.
  • Modernising our CI/CD pipeline for faster, more reliable delivery.
  • Migrating our infrastructure-as-code fully from CloudFormation to Terraform.
  • Extracting and reworking common services to get us ready for our next scale level.

What you'll bring to the team 

  • 5+ years of backend development experience, with a track record of owning significant technical work from ambiguity through to completion.
  • Substantial hands-on ownership of infrastructure, reliability or performance, ideally on a platform or infrastructure team rather than a pure product team.
  • Strong engineering fundamentals that transfer across languages and cloud platforms. We care more about how you think than which stack you've used.
  • Experience designing and scaling distributed systems in cloud-native environments (AWS preferred; strong Azure fundamentals and genuine enthusiasm for the switch work just as well).
  • Comfort with containerised services and infrastructure-as-code (Docker, Terraform; CloudFormation exposure is relevant given our current stack).
  • Confidence writing your own unit and integration tests, as we don't have a dedicated QA function.
  • A project you can talk about in depth: the problem, what you did and the impact it had.
  • Fluent English.

Nice to have 

  • Direct experience with C# (.NET), PostgreSQL, AWS and ECS or Kubernetes: a great fit, though not a hard requirement if your fundamentals are strong.
  • Experience setting up infrastructure-as-code from scratch and working with it day to day, ideally with Terraform, including migrating or consolidating from other approaches (like CloudFormation).
  • Experience with Kafka or other event-driven and streaming systems (Azure Service Bus, RabbitMQ or SQS are good transferable equivalents).
  • Experience owning observability and logging for highly available systems.
  • Hands-on use of AI-assisted development tools (GitHub Copilot, Cursor AI, ChatGPT, Amazon CodeWhisperer) and a genuine interest in AI-driven engineering improvement.
  • Experience mentoring other engineers, and introducing new technology, like AI tooling, to other teams.

 

Culture & Growth

What We Offer 

  • An International Team: Work alongside colleagues from over 20 nationalities. 
  • Growth and Development: 360° feedback reviews, an evolving career framework and an annual learning budget of €1,000+. 
  • Autonomy and Ownership: Great ideas can come from anywhere. We trust you to make decisions and contribute directly. 
  • Real Impact: Join a fast-growing scale-up transforming hospitality. From day one, your work drives real impact. 
  • Fair Pay: Competitive salaries guided by benchmarking data, with recognition for performance and contribution. 
  • Flexible Work: Work from home, the office or a hybrid mix. We focus on results, not clocking hours. 
  • Time Off and Wellbeing: 30 days of vacation and an EGYM Wellpass membership. 
  • Free Public Transport: A fully covered Deutschland Ticket for travel across Germany. 
  • Team Connection: Regular team dinners, company meetups and offsite events. 

How you make an impact joining Apaleo: Joining Apaleo is more than taking on a role. It's about driving real change in the hospitality industry. Your contributions will directly shape our innovative platform, influence company-wide decisions and help redefine the future of hospitality tech. At Apaleo, your voice matters, your ideas are valued and your impact is tangible. Be part of a team where your work fuels progress, collaboration sparks innovation and growth is a shared journey.

We encourage applications from individuals of all backgrounds, regardless of race, colour, religion, gender identity or expression, sex, national origin, age, marital status, disability or any other characteristic protected by applicable law. Your personal data will be handled with the utmost care and in compliance with GDPR and relevant data protection regulations. We celebrate differences and believe that diversity enriches our team and drives innovation.

title: Director Brand Marketing & Community (all genders)
description:
Meet Urban Sports Club

We are among the leading platforms for sports and wellness in Europe, dedicated to inspiring people to live active, healthy lives. With just one membership we offer access to thousands of fitness and wellness experiences across the continent.

But what truly sets us apart? We believe our people are at the heart of everything we do. If you're curious about how we work, what we value and how you might grow with us, explore our Culture Hub & Career Opportunities.

*Big news: Wellhub and Urban Sports Club unite!*
Urban Sports Club is now a proud part of Wellhub, creating a global wellbeing ecosystem. Together, we connect 39,000 corporate clients and 97,000 wellness partners across 18 countries, offering millions of people even more ways to stay active and take care of their health.

 

The opportunity 

We look for a visionary Director of Brand & Community to report directly to our CEO. This is an extraordinary opportunity to shape the next chapter of an already immensely strong brand. As we enjoy incredible brand equity and awareness – particularly in our home market of Germany – you won't be starting from zero. Instead, you will inherit a premium, high-performing base to steer our consumer brand into its next major iteration: moving toward a broader, lifestyle and community-driven positioning.

A core focus of this role will be emphasizing the "Club" in Urban Sports Club. We are a community-driven concept, not just a utility app for solo check-ins. In this hybrid role, you will sit firmly on both the strategic/conceptual side and the operational frontlines. You will champion the evolution of the brand to maximize consumer appeal, while simultaneously developing and executing the concrete marketing strategies that bring our community vision to life. Your most exciting challenge? Internationalization – translating our proven local formula into scalable, culturally resonant consumer strategies for diverse international markets.

What you will do

  • Drive Brand Evolution: Architect the long-term conceptual development and narrative of Urban Sports Club, pivoting the brand toward a holistic, community-centric consumer lifestyle identity. You'll define the brand positioning, value propositions, messaging frameworks and audience strategies in collaboration with our Strategy team.
  • Strengthen the "Club": Ensure campaigns and activations reinforce the community aspect of our brand, creating emotional connections that highlight shared experiences and lifestyle rather than just functional access. We see community as driving both new member acquisition as well as member engagement.
  • Balance Strategy & Execution: Own the brand marketing strategy end-to-end, steering its execution across multi-channel campaigns, PR, Content, and Social Media.
  • Lead Internationalization: Translate, adapt, and scale the core brand strategy across international B2C markets, balancing global consistency with deep local cultural relevance.
  • Steer the Creative Studio & Teams: Oversee and mentor our multi-disciplinary brand teams and internal creative studio, fostering innovation, efficiency, and high-impact creative excellence.
  • Cross-Functional Collaboration: Act as the primary strategic brand stakeholder across the organization, collaborating closely with all marketing leaders to align brand priorities with business objectives.
  • Insights & Budget Management: Efficiently manage the global brand budget while monitoring key health metrics (awareness, sentiment, share of voice) to turn consumer insights into optimized campaign performance.

What you will need to succeed

  • 10+ years of experience leading brand management, marketing, or integrated communications, ideally within lifestyle, community or fast-paced B2C consumer industries.
  • Proven track record of developing scalable international brand strategies and managing large-scale, multi-channel campaigns.
  • Strategic & Execution Hybrid Mindset: Ability to alternate seamlessly between high-level conceptual brand building and concrete, hands-on campaign delivery.
  • Community-First Approach: A strong understanding of consumer brand positioning, audience engagement, and culturally relevant storytelling that builds community.
  • Exceptional Leadership: Strong experience leading cross-functional creative teams, PR specialists, and content creators, alongside managing external agencies.
  • Analytical & Financial Rigor: A data-driven approach to tracking brand performance metrics, translating market research into action, and managing complex global budgets.
  • Language Proficiency: Full fluency in English is required; German language skills are a significant plus.

What's in it for you 

  • Free Urban Sports Club L Pro Membership + Friends and Family Discount: Stay active with free membership, plus discounts for friends and family.
  • Flexible Work Model: Enjoy a hybrid work setup, balancing on-site and remote work options to fit your lifestyle.
  • Extended Remote Work Options: Work up to 120 days remotely within the EU, the UK, and Switzerland, including 30 days outside the EU. You'll also have the option to desk-swap at our other European offices.
  • WorkOUT Life Balance: Take advantage of 30 days of paid vacation annually, plus two additional days for volunteering, flexible working hours, and complimentary access to our mental health provider Open Up.
  • Personal Development: Receive an annual budget of €1,000 for professional growth, with regular internal training sessions and weekly German and English language classes.
  • Engaging Team Culture: Participate in regular team and company events along with wellness initiatives that help you stay productive, healthy, and engaged in a hybrid work environment.

Urban Sports Club is committed to providing a friendly, safe, and welcoming environment for everyone who applies for a position or already works with us, regardless of their sports preferences, gender, gender identity and expression, sexual orientation, disability, physical appearance, body size, race, age, or religion (or lack thereof).

title: Data Center Architect
description:
Role Profile

Job Title: Data Centre Architect

Reports to: Head of Data Centre Development

Location: UK hybrid

Company Overview:

Radiant is redefining how AI infrastructure is built.

We design and operate AI-native cloud platforms engineered for sovereignty, performance, and scale. Our infrastructure powers GPU-native workloads, multi-tenant control planes, and high-performance AI systems designed for the most demanding environments.

We are not building a generic cloud. We are building purpose-built AI infrastructure — from powered land, to compute, to software.

As we scale, we’re building this organisation from the ground up. We’re looking for people who’d rather build the playbook than inherit one — who are comfortable doing the work themselves as well as directing others, and who can adapt as fast as our strategy does. This is a startup model: attitude and adaptability matter more to us than years of experience or the size of team you’ve previously managed.

This is a senior individual contributor role with authority to sign off technical schedules, working with cluster and network architects, NVIDIA and other OEM engineers, colocation provider engineering and sales teams, and the internal Procurement, Legal, Finance and Site Operations teams.

What You’ll Do

You will be the single technical authority between our GPU-as-a-service business and the colocation providers that host our NVIDIA clusters. You turn cluster architecture and OEM requirements into a precise, contractable statement of work (SOW) for the data centre white space, then hold the provider to it through design, installation and acceptance.

We are growing from tens of megawatts to hundreds, on rack-scale liquid-cooled platforms at 130 kW per rack and rising to 200 kW and beyond. Mistakes in power, cooling or fibre specification show up as stranded capacity, delayed cluster delivery and disputes, so the role carries real commercial weight.

Key Responsibilities

Technical negotiation with colocation providers

  • Lead technical due diligence on candidate sites: power availability and energisation dates, redundancy topology, liquid-cooling capability, floor loading, rack logistics, fibre and meet-me access.

  • Negotiate the technical schedules of the colocation agreement with commercial and legal: capacity and density commitments, power and cooling SLAs, temperature and flow envelopes, metering, expansion rights, change control and remedies.

  • Challenge provider claims with evidence: single-line diagrams, P&IDs, load-bank and commissioning records, reference customers.

Specification & SOW

  • Work with cluster architects and OEMs (NVIDIA first) to capture rack, power, cooling, network and layout requirements, and keep them current across product generations.

  • Write and own the technical SOW for white-space fitout: containment and cooling interfaces, power distribution to rack, structured cabling and pathways, rack and POD layout, security zoning, labelling and records.

  • Define clear scope boundaries and responsibilities between us, the colocation provider, OEMs and installation contractors, with no gaps and no overlaps.

  • Maintain a requirements baseline with traceability from OEM document, to SOW clause, to acceptance test.

Design, installation & acceptance

  • Review provider and contractor designs, shop drawings and method statements against the SOW; run design reviews and close findings.

  • Define acceptance: factory and site tests, liquid flush and cleanliness, power quality, thermal performance at full load, fibre loss, burn-in, and the evidence pack needed for each gate.

  • Attend key witness tests and sign off, or reject, completion of each phase before hardware is energised.

  • Manage technical change requests and variations, and advise on cost and schedule impact.

Knowledge & standards

  • Build reusable reference designs, SOW templates and a site-scoring framework so each new deployment starts from a proven baseline.

  • Track the roadmap: higher rack densities, 800 VDC distribution, new cooling classes and optics, and tell the business early what it means for sites already contracted.

Deliverables You Own:

  • Site technical assessment: Scored, evidence-based report per candidate site, comparable across providers, with risks and mitigations.

  • Technical schedules to the colocation agreement: Measurable commitments, tested in acceptance, with remedies agreed by legal.

  • Cluster white-space SOW: Complete enough that a contractor can price and build without asking us questions; traceable to OEM requirements.

  • Reference designs and layouts: Rack, row and POD layouts, power and cooling single-line and P&ID level interfaces, fibre pathways and densities.

  • Acceptance test plan and evidence pack: Pass and fail criteria set before work starts; signed results per gate.

  • Requirements baseline and change log: One current version of the truth, with every variation recorded and costed.

  • Risk and issues register: Technical risks to schedule and capacity, with owners and dates.

Working Relationships:

  • Cluster and network architects: You translate their cluster design into facility requirements, and they rely on you to say what a site can and cannot carry.

  • OEMs, mainly NVIDIA: You are the facility-side counterpart; you obtain, interpret and challenge site-requirement documents.

  • Colocation providers: Day-to-day technical counterpart through negotiation, build and acceptance.

  • Procurement, legal and finance: You provide the technical substance of commercial terms and the impact of variations.

  • Site operations and deployment teams: You hand over a clean specification and acceptance evidence, and take back lessons learned.

What You Bring:

  • 8 or more years in data centre design, delivery or technical consulting, including at least 3 years on high-density (50 kW per rack or more) or liquid-cooled deployments.

  • Direct experience writing or reviewing technical specifications and SOWs for white-space fitout, and managing contractors against them to acceptance.

  • Strong working knowledge of data centre power: MV and LV distribution, UPS and generator topologies, redundancy models (N+1, 2N, distributed), busway and rack power, metering and power quality.

  • Strong working knowledge of cooling: direct-to-chip liquid cooling, CDUs, facility and technology loops, warm-water and dry-cooler designs, fluid quality and flushing, leak detection and containment.

  • Working knowledge of structured cabling and pathways for large GPU fabrics (single-mode optics, high fibre counts, InfiniBand and Ethernet physical layers), and of rack and POD layouts.

  • Familiarity with NVIDIA rack-scale platforms (GB200 or GB300 class, or later) and their facility requirements, and the ability to read OEM site-requirement documents critically.

  • Proven ability to run technical negotiations with colocation or construction counterparties, and to explain trade-offs to commercial, legal and executive audiences.

  • Command of standards such as EN 50600 and the Uptime Tier framework, ASHRAE TC 9.9 liquid-cooling guidance, and commissioning practice (levels 1 to 5).

  • Excellent written communication: you produce clear, unambiguous contract-grade documents.

Preferred Skills (Nice to Have):

  • Experience at a hyperscaler, neocloud or colocation provider on the operator or customer side.

  • Experience with 800 VDC or other DC distribution, large battery storage, or power smoothing for AI load swings.

  • Chartered engineer status or equivalent; recognised data centre credentials (for example CDCP, CDFOM, Uptime ATD or AOS).

  • Familiarity with BIM, digital-twin tools and requirements-management tools.

  • Willingness to travel up to 30% to sites in the UK, Europe and the US.

Success Measures:

  • First 90 days: Audit current colocation contracts and SOWs and list technical gaps; publish a requirements baseline for the current NVIDIA platform; take over technical lead on one live negotiation; agree the site-scoring framework with the cluster architects.

  • 6 months: One complete SOW issued and priced with no material scope disputes; acceptance plan agreed with the provider before build starts; reusable SOW template adopted by the team.

  • 12 months: Every new site contracted on the template with traceable requirements; clusters accepted on schedule with no facility-caused performance issues; fewer late variations and a measurable cut in time from site shortlist to signed technical schedule.

Qualities we look for:

  • Set the standard: Every single day, you spot opportunities to constructively shake things up.

  • Inspire the change: There’s no blueprint for the future. You’ll embrace challenges and change.

  • You’re real and you’re true to yourself: We cherish and celebrate diversity so you’ll feel right at home whoever you are and whoever you’re talking to, you treat everyone the same.

  • Get stuck in: You’d rather be building than overseeing. Our strategy will keep evolving, and so will you — attitude and adaptability matter more to us than a fixed playbook or a big team behind you.

Package & Process:

  • Employment type: Full-time, permanent.

  • Travel: Up to 30%.

  • Interview process:

    Talent Screening > Hiring Manager Screen > Technical Interview > Final with the Head of Data Centre Development.

We are an equal opportunities employer and welcome applications from all backgrounds.

description:
Odin is building the investment infrastructure for the future of private markets.
We believe capital is one of the most powerful tools for shaping the world - and more people should know how to put it to work. Our mission is to make it radically easier to raise and deploy capital, so that anyone, anywhere, can back the companies and ideas they believe in.

This includes household names like ElevenLabs, OpenAI, SpaceX, xAI, Anduril, etc. but also new companies creating everything from synthetic brains to small nuclear reactors.

 

Why we're hiring

  • We are automating a decades old part of the financial services industry. AI pilled builders like you are the beating heart of this plan, because LLMs & agents allow us to turn this services business entirely into software.

  • This is a product role, and your product is how Odin operates. Think of it as our ghostbuster: every operational problem lands with you, you decide what gets fixed, and you ship most of the fixes yourself rather than writing tickets for someone else.

  • We're post-PMF, fast-growing, and rolling out new products (fund admin) & geographies (USA). Customer & deal volume is climbing fast.

  • Today we're on track for roughly 700 deals a year, with a team of ~20, and we'll process $500m-$750m of investment in 2026 alone.

  • The next goal is 7,000 deals a year and billions in annual investment flows.

  • We believe this can be achieved with a team of around 50 people. But it will only be possible if we turn human-driven services workflows into software.

  • Odin's operations run on around 50 processes, some code and some people, and plenty still held together by spreadsheets. Your job is to take each one apart, question why it exists, then rebuild it or kill it.

  • The simplest way to think about it: the numerator is how many deals we close, the denominator is what each deal costs us to run. You'll focus on the denominator, and the right person won't be able to stop themselves thinking about the numerator too.

  • We expect the right hire to be spending more time in Claude Code than in Excel, email or anything else.

     

What you'll own

  • Triage: Every operational problem comes to you before it reaches product and engineering. For each one you decide: scope it so precisely that engineering knows exactly what to build, or build it yourself.

  • Cost per deal: There will be big early wins where a whole process can be ripped out and replaced. After that, doubling ops efficiency comes from 150 small changes, and you'll be the one making them.

  • Automation: You'll sit with the deal operations team, learn each workflow end to end, then build what replaces it. Most of what you ship you'll build without engineering. What does go to them arrives simple, scoped and usually with a working prototype attached.

  • Deleting things and saying no: You decide what belongs in our processes and what doesn't. If a request from sales doesn't scale and isn't highly profitable we don't do it. If a way of working exists for no good reason, you kill it.

  • The ops team: You'll lead the core deal operations team, deciding where their time goes while you rebuild the work around them.

     

What we're looking for

  • You build, not buy: Clear evidence, at work or in your own time, that you've built real solutions with AI with no budget and no engineers. Buying a tool or setting up workflows in Sheets doesn't count. We want to see what you've shipped in Claude Code or similar.

  • Founder or product DNA: You've founded something, been early on a founding team, or worked as a product manager. That usually means four or more years of experience and a track record of finishing what you start.

  • Systems thinker: You look at any process the way a good product manager looks at a product: What's the job? Why are we doing this at all? What's the smallest, simplest system that achieves the goal? You think about the whole business, not just your corner of it.
    A lot of what happens in fund admin is inherited convention, an industry "given", or a constraint of some third party. You should find it physically difficult to accept any of that.

  • In the details and extremely on top of things: You understand every single aspect of our systems end to end. You close loops, you chase, you push hard to get things done.

  • Numerate: Comfortable with financial mechanics, strong mental arithmetic. You'll be automating a lot of numerical work - carry, allocations, fee calculations, distributions, and the edge cases that make all of them interesting.

  • Big plus: regulated financial services background: Fund administration, custody, payments, brokerage, audit, tax or another back office function. Useful, but not required. We care much more about the traits you have and the things you can build than specific skills or experience on your CV.

     

How we work

There are five things we care about deeply:

  1. Reason from the ground up
    Seek to understand what is true by always asking why. Do not trust convention or experts.

  2. Speed begets speed
    We work fast. Speed compounds, it's the best form of defensibility, and it's energising to be around. If you work slowly, or tolerate slow work around you, you do not belong at Odin.

  3. Take ownership
    Do not wait for permission to do things. Find the answer, force the thing into existence and hold others to an extremely high standard - the same standard you hold yourself to.

  4. Brutal honesty
    If work doesn't meet the bar, people need to hear it, and the right people want to.

  5. Truly excellent customer service
    Be a stickler for detail in every single interaction a customer has with us, and always strive to make this experience better, smoother, faster.

     

This role is probably not for you if

  • You'd rather write specs and hand tickets to engineers than build the thing yourself;

  • You prefer close management of your responsibilities;

  • You are risk-averse;

  • You want a 9-5;

  • You take yourself too seriously;

  • You care about working for a company that's raised lots of money rather than one that's extremely capital efficient and focused on building a profitable giant that has a positive economic impact

     

Salary

£90k - £120k base, plus a meaningful equity grant. We're flexible on the mix of cash and equity.

 

Hiring process

Three stages, usually inside two weeks, with detailed feedback within 24 hours of each one. A call with our Head of People, an in-person session with the founders where you solve a real Odin problem end to end with AI, then a final with the founders. The last two can run on the same day.

 

Location & ways of working

We're a London-based team. This role works closely with the founders, product and the wider ops team, and the speed we run at makes that much easier in-person. At least three days a week in the office.

title: Quadrants: Compiler Lead
description:
What Quadrants is

Quadrants is an open-source translation layer that turns ordinary Python into optimized machine code at runtime, across CPU (Arm64, x86) and GPU (AMDGPU, CUDA, Metal, Vulkan) backends. CUDA is the primary target, with x86 the strong runner-up, especially for real-time simulation. The others drive adoption and support fast prototyping for research.

The ambition is explicit: build the best “Python compiler” in the world for physics and performance-critical numerical computing. We are fully committed to it, and we intend to beat leading alternatives like Nvidia Warp, Numba, or Triton.

It’s a standalone project with its own roadmap, built in the open. Genesis, our physics simulator, is its first and top-priority user, the source of its hardest workloads and its benchmarks. But Quadrants is general-purpose infrastructure for anyone writing performance-critical numerical Python, not an internal tool that happens to be public.

The bet: high-performance code should feel natural to write. Engineers write plain Python in a NumPy or PyTorch style, and Quadrants makes it fast.

The role

You own Quadrants end to end: the API, the IR and lowering, the optimization passes, the numerical primitives, and the roadmap.

Our ultimate objective: engineers write for readability and maintainability, never for performance. They write the version of an algorithm they are most comfortable with, and Quadrants rebuilds it into kernels that run as if an expert had hand-tuned them. Performance is the compiler’s job, not theirs. Getting there is a frontier problem, part research and part engineering, and we intend to define the state of the art on it, relentlessly pushing the limit further.

It calls for two things at once: the low-level GPU and compiler skill to make a single kernel optimal, and the ability to keep the whole system coherent as it grows.

The core tradeoff is settled: usability comes first. When usability and performance collide, usability wins, unless the cost is severe. We will limit what the system supports to go fast (static shapes and fixed-size allocation baked into kernels, say), but never the convenience of the API itself. Experts who want maximum performance and full control over the generated code get lower-level escape hatches, down to inline assembly, C, or PTX.

Your mandate is to build the best open-source Python compiler for physics simulation out there. No limit on what that takes. If it means replacing the entire engine, your call. Either way, you keep Quadrants healthy and unblocking the company in the meantime.

What you’ll own

  • API & authoring experience. The surface that physics and numerical-computing engineers write against, and, as an open-source library, the product’s face to the world. Idiomatic, natural to Python users, never a separate language bolted onto Python. Clean decorators, legible constraints, sharp errors, real escape hatches.

  • IR, lowering & backends. A stable IR that lowers to multiple backends, with room to grow and the door kept open for differentiable simulation. Today the computation graph is expressed through Quadrants’ own constructs. Recovering it automatically from ordinary Python is hard, and a long-term goal rather than today’s reality.

  • Optimization. Turn naive code into strong execution plans: vectorization, register and shared-memory usage, barriers and atomics, cooperative threading, dead-buffer and redundant-traffic elimination, dropping needless synchronization. Move low-level optimization off users and into the platform.

  • Primitives. Cholesky, eigendecomposition, matmul, reductions, solver kernels. Each owned with its correctness, benchmarks, and regression tracking.

  • Watching Genesis and the compiler together. Hunt for performance wins on both sides, in Genesis and in Quadrants itself. Propose API changes that cut duplication, improve readability, and reduce platform-specific special-casing. Less to maintain, more that simply works.

  • The project as a product. Benchmark real workloads, track performance over time, catch regressions early. Stay close to users (Genesis first), find friction and missing abstractions, drive adoption, set direction.

Who you are

You reason about whole systems and have taste for where complexity should live. You measure before you optimize, and you reach for memory traffic and launch overhead before FLOPs. You have opinions about API design. You write tests and benchmarks as you go, not afterward.

The ground that judgment stands on:

  • GPU. What optimal looks like and why: access patterns, registers, shared memory, barriers, atomics, threading. CPU intuition a plus.

  • Python & API taste. Idiomatic Python. A feel for what’s natural to Python users. APIs that free users rather than constrain them.

  • Compilers. The path from authoring to kernels (IR, lowering, optimization), weighed against maintainability.

And how you work: proactive and largely self-directed. You fetch context across the company instead of waiting for it. You’re comfortable talking to the engineers who use what you build, and at ease designing in the open for users you’ll never meet. Ready to grow into leading a small team (a couple of people, near term).

What great looks like

People adopt Quadrants from outside Genesis. Engineers write clearer code with less boilerplate. Kernels keep getting faster. Performance is tracked, not guessed. The architecture gets easier to extend, not harder.

What we’re uncompromising about

How you work is up to you. What matters is that your ownership grows over time: blind spots shrink, the parts you can vouch for expand, technical debt goes down, the core stays sound.

That takes treating understanding as real work, not overhead. You read and challenge the codebase instead of just stacking features on it. You take nothing you did not write for granted. You watch the competition and what’s coming next, and you bring it in and ship it.

Use AI agents if they help. They are productivity tools, not code owners. You are.

title: ML Compiler & System
description:
What Quadrants is

Quadrants is an open-source translation layer that turns ordinary Python into optimized machine code at runtime, across CPU (Arm64, x86) and GPU (AMDGPU, CUDA, Metal, Vulkan) backends. CUDA is the primary target, with x86 the strong runner-up, especially for real-time simulation. The others drive adoption and support fast prototyping for research.

The ambition is explicit: build the best “Python compiler” in the world for physics and performance-critical numerical computing. We are fully committed to it, and we intend to beat leading alternatives like Nvidia Warp, Numba, or Triton.

It’s a standalone project with its own roadmap, built in the open. Genesis, our physics simulator, is its first and top-priority user, the source of its hardest workloads and its benchmarks. But Quadrants is general-purpose infrastructure for anyone writing performance-critical numerical Python, not an internal tool that happens to be public.

The bet: high-performance code should feel natural to write. Engineers write plain Python in a NumPy or PyTorch style, and Quadrants makes it fast.

 

The role

You own Quadrants end to end: the API, the IR and lowering, the optimization passes, the numerical primitives, and the roadmap.

Our ultimate objective: engineers write for readability and maintainability, never for performance. They write the version of an algorithm they are most comfortable with, and Quadrants rebuilds it into kernels that run as if an expert had hand-tuned them. Performance is the compiler’s job, not theirs. Getting there is a frontier problem, part research and part engineering, and we intend to define the state of the art on it, relentlessly pushing the limit further.

It calls for two things at once: the low-level GPU and compiler skill to make a single kernel optimal, and the ability to keep the whole system coherent as it grows.

The core tradeoff is settled: usability comes first. When usability and performance collide, usability wins, unless the cost is severe. We will limit what the system supports to go fast (static shapes and fixed-size allocation baked into kernels, say), but never the convenience of the API itself. Experts who want maximum performance and full control over the generated code get lower-level escape hatches, down to inline assembly, C, or PTX.

 

What you’ll own

  • API & authoring experience. The surface that physics and numerical-computing engineers write against, and, as an open-source library, the product’s face to the world. Idiomatic, natural to Python users, never a separate language bolted onto Python. Clean decorators, legible constraints, sharp errors, real escape hatches.

  • IR, lowering & backends. A stable IR that lowers to multiple backends, with room to grow and the door kept open for differentiable simulation. Today the computation graph is expressed through Quadrants’ own constructs. Recovering it automatically from ordinary Python is hard, and a long-term goal rather than today’s reality.

  • Optimization. Turn naive code into strong execution plans: vectorization, register and shared-memory usage, barriers and atomics, cooperative threading, dead-buffer and redundant-traffic elimination, dropping needless synchronization. Move low-level optimization off users and into the platform.

  • Primitives. Cholesky, eigendecomposition, matmul, reductions, solver kernels. Each owned with its correctness, benchmarks, and regression tracking.

  • Watching Genesis and the compiler together. Hunt for performance wins on both sides, in Genesis and in Quadrants itself. Propose API changes that cut duplication, improve readability, and reduce platform-specific special-casing. Less to maintain, more that simply works.

  • The project as a product. Benchmark real workloads, track performance over time, catch regressions early. Stay close to users (Genesis first), find friction and missing abstractions, drive adoption, set direction.

Who you are

You reason about whole systems and have taste for where complexity should live. You measure before you optimize, and you reach for memory traffic and launch overhead before FLOPs. You have opinions about API design. You write tests and benchmarks as you go, not afterward.

The ground that judgment stands on:

  • GPU. What optimal looks like and why: access patterns, registers, shared memory, barriers, atomics, threading. CPU intuition a plus.

  • Python & API taste. Idiomatic Python. A feel for what’s natural to Python users. APIs that free users rather than constrain them.

  • Compilers. The path from authoring to kernels (IR, lowering, optimization), weighed against maintainability.

And how you work: proactive and largely self-directed. You fetch context across the company instead of waiting for it. You’re comfortable talking to the engineers who use what you build, and at ease designing in the open for users you’ll never meet. Ready to grow into leading a small team (a couple of people, near term).

 

What great looks like

People adopt Quadrants from outside Genesis. Engineers write clearer code with less boilerplate. Kernels keep getting faster. Performance is tracked, not guessed. The architecture gets easier to extend, not harder.

 

What we’re uncompromising about

How you work is up to you. What matters is that your ownership grows over time: blind spots shrink, the parts you can vouch for expand, technical debt goes down, the core stays sound.

That takes treating understanding as real work, not overhead. You read and challenge the codebase instead of just stacking features on it. You take nothing you did not write for granted. You watch the competition and what’s coming next, and you bring it in and ship it.

Use AI agents if they help. They are productivity tools, not code owners. You are.

  • Set and own IT's operating rhythm: support tooling, SLAs, and the metrics that show whether the function is improving.

  • Manage the IT budget and vendor portfolio - evaluating spend, negotiating commercial terms, ensuring that we’re operating efficiently and running a SaaS estate that spans across multiple departments.

L’histoire de Theodo et son succès

Depuis 2009, Theodo conçoit, développe et déploie des produits digitaux ingénieux. Notre approche : le meilleur de la technologie, au service de la création de valeur, porté par l'approche Lean.

Notre approche unique est fondée sur 3 principes :

  • nous avons développé des expertises reconnues dans les technologies clés de la conception et du développement produit;
  • quelle que soit l’étape du projet, notre priorité à chaque décision est la création de valeur pour nos clients;
  • nous recrutons les meilleurs talents digitaux et cultivons leur ingéniosité grâce à l’approche lean.

En 15 ans, nous sommes devenus un groupe de plus de 700 Theodoers, organisé en entités spécialisées par technologie (Apps, Cloud, Data & AI) et par industrie (Fintech, Govtech, Healthtech, Consumer Products Goods). En 2025, le groupe génère 100M€ de CA.



Tes missions

La santé se digitalise. Les données de vie réelle explosent. Elles facilitent le soin et accélèrent la recherche, notamment via les entrepôts de données de santé.

Ces données sont extrêmement sensibles et réglementées. Nos clients ont donc besoin de notre expertise pour bâtir des applications sur des architectures Cloud conformes à la réglementation HDS. L'arrivée des LLM ajoute un défi : exposer ces données à des agents pour aider les soignants et les patients, sans jamais transiger sur la sécurité.

Dans notre équipe, tu travailleras sur des sujets concrets, au service du soin et de la recherche. Des projets utiles, pour des produits qui comptent.

Ton rôle : concevoir, convaincre et déployer

Ta mission est avant tout opérationnelle. Tu conçois, tu présentes et tu mets en place des architectures Cloud qui répondent aux besoins fonctionnels, de sécurité et de conformité de nos clients.

Concrètement :

  • Avant-vente : traduire un besoin en architecture adaptée, et convaincre le client que c’est la plus ingénieuse pour le projet.
  • Déploiement : infrastructure as code, de bout en bout.
  • Audit : conformité HDS et bonnes pratiques des standards Cloud.
  • Développement d’assets : agents, boilerplates, projets open source.
